MESSAGE from his Majesty, by Mr. distort. Deputy Gentleman Usher of the Black Rod: Mr. Speaker,

The King commands this Honourable House to attend him immediately in the House of Peers.

A Petition of William CuUiford Esquire, was presented Corse Castle to the House, and read; setting forth, That, a late Election. Election for a Burgess to serve in Parliament for Corse Castle, in the County of Doi'set, being declared void as to /iichard Femmes Esquire, and the Petitioner, a new Writ issued for another Ejection, and they again stood Candidates; but Henry Dackombe, the Mayor, openly declared himself in favour of Mr. Founts, and arbitrarily refused to poll for the Petitioner many legal Voters, and admitted several Persons to poll for Mr. femmes who had no right to vote; yet, notwithstanding such indirect Practices, the Petitioner had a great Majority of legal Votes, and ought to have been returned, the Majority appearing upon casting up of the Poll; but the said Mayor declared he would return Mr. Femmes, for all that: Nor could the Petitioner prevail with the Mayor to enter upon a Scrutiny of those which were queried, and agreed to be examined after the Poll; but, in manifest Breach of his Trust, and Prejudice of the Petitioner, he proclaimed Mr. Fozvnes as duly elected: And praying the Justice and Equity of the House in the Premises.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the Committee of Privileges and Elections:

And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the same, with their Opinion therein to the House.

A Petition of several of the Magistrates, Burgesses, and Ditta. Inhabitants, of the said Borough of Corse Cetstle, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That, a new Writ issuing for electing a Burgess to serve in Parliament for the said Borough, in the room of William Cull ford Esquire, whose late Election, in Competition with Richard Fozvnes Esquire, was adjudged void, the said Mr. CuUiford and Mr. Fencnes stood Candidates again:

But the Mayor, resolving, right or wrong, to carry on the Election for Mr. Fownts, did not only refuse to poll a great Number of legal Electors for Mr. Culliford, who were admitted in all former Elections; but admitted others to poll for Mr. Fownes, who had no Right, and never were polled before: And though the Petitioners often desired the Mayor to proceed in this as in former Elections, yet he would not; but arbitrarily carried 011 the Election in behalf of Mr. Femmes, without the least Regard to the Peoples Right; and yet Mr. CuUiford had a much greater Number of good Votes; but the said Mayor peremptorily declared Mr. Fozvnes as duty elected, and has returned him, in Violation of the Rights of the said Borough, which are in Danger of being totally subverted, as to Elections, without the Relief of this House:

And praying their Consideration in the Premises; and that the said Mayor may be brought to answer such hb illegal Practices.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the Committee of Privileges and Elections:

And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the same, with their Opinion therein, to the House.

A Petition of Shadrack Vincent Esquire, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That, at the last Election of Burgesses to serve in this Parliament for the Borough of Fowey in the County of Cornwall, the Petitioner stood a Candidate, and ought to have been returned a Burgess; because a great Majority of the legal Voters appeared and voted for him: But Jonathan Tincomb, Port-reve of the said Borough, arbitrarily, and contrary to the ancient Rights of the said Borough, refused to poll the Petitioner's Voices, who had almost all the qualified Voters; and wrongfully returned Sir Bevil Grenville, and Thomas Vivian Esquire; declaring he would not return the Petitioner, though he had never so many Voices; but that he would return Sir Bevil Grenville, if he had but Four: And the Portreve being told, That the Petitioner might recover Damages against him for such his false Return, answered, That he hoped to get 500l. by the Bargain, and would not return the Petitioner, though the Majority signed and sealed an Indenture for returning him as One of their Burgesses; and many other ill Practices were used in behalf of the sitting Members: And praying such Relief in the Premises, as the House shall think fit.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the Committee of Privileges and Elections: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the same, with their Opinion therein, to the House.

taer A Petition of divers Inhabitants of the ancient City and Libertiesof Westminsterpresented to the House, and read; setting forth. That a Court of Conscience within the City of London, for determining small Debts under Forty Shillings, hath been found of great Advantage to the poorer Sort of Freemen: That the City and Liberties of Westminster are very populous, and the Poor daily increase; and, for want of a Court of Conscience, many vexatious Suits and Actions arise for small Debts, the Expences whereof are greater than the Debts, to the Ruin of their Families, and the Filling of Prisons with miserable Debtors: And that, in the First Year of his now Majesty, an Act passed for erecting the like Courts of Conscience in the Cities of Bristoll and Gloucester, which had the designed Effect: The Petitioners therefore pray, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to erect a Court of Conscience within the said City and Liberties, for determining all Matters of Debt, and Actions upon the Case, under the Value of Forty Shillings; it being conceived for the general Benefit of all Sorts of People inhabiting within the said City and Liberties.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That it will equally conduce to the continuing and establishing an entire Confidence between the King and this House, That his Majesty will be pleased to shew Marks of his Displeasure towards such Persons as have or shall presume to misrepresent the Proceedings of this Parliament to his Majesty.

Resolved', That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That it will equally conduce to the continuing and establishing an entire Confidence between the King and his People, That Care be taken to prevent and discourage all false Rumours and Reports, reflecting on his Majesty, and his Government ,* whereby to create any Misunderstanding between Him and his Subjects.

Mr. Conyers reported from the Committee, to whom it was referred to draw up an humble Address to be presented to his Majesty, upon the Resolutions of the House of Tuesday last, That they had drawn up an Address accordingly; which they had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; anil afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz. '

Most gracious Sovereign,

We, your Majesty's most dutiful and loyal Subjects, the Commons in Parliament assembled, being highly sensible, that nothing is more necessary for the Peace and Welfare of this Kingdom, the quieting the Minds of your People, and disappointing the Designs of your Enemies, than a mutual and entire Confidence between your Majesty and your Parliament, do esteem it our greatest Misfortune, That, after having so amply provided for the Security of your Majesty, and your Government, both by Sea and Land, any Jealousy or Distrust hath been raised, of our Duty and Affections to your Sacred Majesty and your People; and beg leave humbly to represent to your Majesty, That it will greatly conduce to the continuing and establishing an entire Confidence between your Majesty and your Parliament, that you will be pleased to shew Marks of your high Displeasure towards all such Persons, wlx/have, or shall presume to misrepresent their Proceedings to your Majesty.

And your Commons, having likewise a due Sense of the great Care and Concern your Majesty has always expressed, for preserving and maintaining the Religion, Rights, and Liberties of your People, in Defence of which your Majesty hath so often exposed your'Royal Person, will use their utmost Care and Endeavour to prevent and discourage all false Rumours and Reports, reflecting upon your Majesty and your- Government, whereby to create any Misunderstanding between you and your Subjects.

Several Amendments were proposed to be made: Which, upon the Question severally put thereupon, were agreed unto by the House; viz.t

The Words " Most gracious Sovereign," and " high," were added.

Resolved, That the said Address, so amended, be agreed unto.

Resolved, That the said Address be presented to his Majesty by the whole House.

Ordered, That such Members of this House as are of his Majesty's most Honourable Privy Council, do humbly know his Majesty's Pleasure when he will be attended by this House.

The House, according to Ord$r, resolved itself into a Committee of the whole House, to consider of the present State and Condition of the Trade of England.

Prayers.

A PETITION of the Company of the Royal Fish- Royal ery of England was presented to the House, and Fishery, read; setting forth, That King Charles the Second, in the Twenty-ninth Year of his Reign, did, by his Letters Patents, incorporate the said Company, by the Name of the Royal Fishery of England; who have ever since, at great Expence, and Loss of Time, endeavoured to regain and establish the Fishery in the British Seas; and have employed several Sums of Money in making Experiments therein; by which they have gotten good Information and Experience: Whereupon, about Three Years since, they opened Books for taking Subscriptions to the Value of Three hundred thousand Pounds for carrying on so great and advantageous a Work; and thereupon Subscriptions were made; but the Subscribers were unwilling to pay in their Money, unless they can be established by Act of Parliament: And praying the House to take such reasonable Consideration in the Premises, as may tend to the Regaining of the said Fishery, the Encouragement of the Subscribers, and the Good of the Kingdom in general.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the Committee of the whole House, who are to consider of the State and Condition of the Trade of England: And that they do consider of the best Ways and Means for the Improvement of the Fishery of England; and report their Opinions therein, to the House.

Ordered, That Mr. Speaker do issue his warrant to the Dartra Clerk of the Crown, to make out a new Writ, for the Writ, electing a Burgess to serve in this present Parliament for the Borough of Clifton-Dartmouth-Hardnesse in the County of Devon, in the room of Sir Joseph Herne Knight, deceased.

The Copy of the Commission from the Admiralty.

By the Commissioners for executing the Office of Lord High Admiral of England, Ireland, &c. WHEREAS by Commission under the Great Seal of England, bearing Date the 26th Day of June 1689. or any Three or more of us, are required and authorized to grant Commissions, unto such Persons as we deem fitly qualified in that behalf for the apprehending, seizing, and taking such Ships, Vessels, and Goods, belonging to the French King, And his Subjects, and Inhabitants within the Dominions of the said French King; and such other Ships, Vessels, and Goods, as are or shall be liable to Confiscation; with other Powers in the said Commission expressed: These are therefore to will and require you forthwith to cause a Commission, or Letter of Marque or Reprizal, to be issued out of the High Court of Admiralty of England, untoCaptain William Kidd, Commander of the Adventure Gaily, Burden 287 Tons, 34 Guns, and 70 Men, to set forth in warlike Manner the said Ship called the Adventure Gaily, w hereof the said Captain William Kidd is Commander, and to apprehend, seize, and 'take, the Ships, Vessels, and Goods, belonging to the French King, or his Subjects, or Inhabitants within the Dominions of the said French King; and such other Ships, Vessels, and Goods, as are, or shall be, liable to Confiscation; according to the said Commission granted unto us for that Purpose, and certain Articles and Instructions under her late Majesty's Signet and Sign Manual, dated the 2d of May 1693, a Copy whereof remains with you; and according to the Course of the Court of Admiralty, and Laws of Nations: And you are therein to insert a Clause, injoining the said Captain Wm. Kidd to keep an exact Journal of his Proceedings; and therein particularly to take notice of all Prizes, which shall be taken by him, the vNature of such Prizes, the Time and Place of their being taken, and the Value of them, as near as he can judge; as also the Station, Motion, and Strength of the Enemy, as well as he can discover by the best Intelligence he can get: Of which he is, from time to time, as he shall have an Opportunity, to transmit an Account for us to our Secretary, and to keep a Correspondence with him by all Opportunities, that shall present: Provided always, That, before you issue such Commission, Security be given thereupon, according as is directed in her late Majesty's Instructions afore-mentioned; as also, That a Recognizance, or sufficient.....not exceeding 500l. be

entered into, obliging him not to carry in the said Ship more than One half of her Complement of Seamen; but that all the rest of her Company be Landmen; and that he do, at the End of the Voyage, give in to the Secretary of the Admiralty a perfect List, in Columns, of his Ship's Company, expressing their Names, Qualities, Ages, Places of Abode, and whether married or single Men; and also, That he do give Security strictly to conform himself to the Regulations contained in their Majesties Proclamation of the 12th of July 1694, concerning Colours to be worn on board Ships. This Commission to continue in Force till further Order; for which this shall be your Warrant. Given under our Hands and the Seal of the Office of Admiralty, this Tenth Day of December, 1695.

J. Lowther.

The said Copy of the Commission under the Great Seal. WILLIAM R.

William the Third, by the Grace of God, King of England, Scotland, France, and Ireland, Defender of the Faith, T o our Trusty and well-bcloved Captain William Kidd, Commander of the Ship Adventure Gaily, or to the Commander of the said Ship for the Time being; Greeting. Whereas we are informed, That Captain Thomas Too, John Ireland Captain Thomas Wake, Captain William Maze or Mace, and other our Subjects, Natives or Inhabitants of New England, New York, and elsewhere, in our Plantations in America, have associated themselves with divers other wicked and ill-disposed Persons; and do, against the Laws of Nations, daily commit many great Piracies, Robberies, and Depredations, upon the Seas in the Parts of America, and in other Parts, to the great Hindrance and Discouragement of Trade and Navigation, and to the Danger and Hurt of our loving Subjects, our Allies, and all others, navigating the Seas, upon their lawful Occasions: Now know ye, That we, being desirous to prevent the aforesaid Mischiefs, and, as far as in us lies, to bring the said Pirates, Free-booters, and Sea Rovers, to Justice, have thought fit, and do hereby give and grant unto you, the said Captain William Kidd, to whom our Commissioners for executing the Office of our Lord High Admiral have granted a Commission, as a private Man of War, bearing Date the Eleventh Day of December 1695.; and unto the Officers, Mariners, and others, which shall be under your Command; full Power and Authority to apprehend, seize, and take into your Custody, as well the said Captain Tho. Too, John Ireland, Captain Thomas Wake, William Maze alias Mace, as such Pirates, Free-booters, and Sea Rovers, being either own Subjects, or ot\other Nations associated with them, which you shall meet with upon the said Coasts or Seas of America, or in any other Seas or Parts, with their Ships and Vessels; and also such Merchandizes, Money, Goods, and Wares, as shall be found on board, or with them; in case they shall willingly yield themselves; but if they will not submit without fighting, then you are by Force to compel them to yield: And we do also require you to bring, or cause to be brought, such Pirates, Free-booters, and Sea Rovers, as you shall seize, to a legal Tryal, to the end they maybe proceeded against according to the Law in such Cases: And we do hereby charge and command all our Officers, Ministers, and other our loving Subjects whatsoever, to be aiding and assisting to you in the Premises: And we do hereby injoin you to keep an exact Journal of your Proceedings in the Execution of the Premises; and therein to set down the Names of such Pirates, and of their Officers and Company, and the Names of such Ships and Vessels, as you shall, by virtue of these Preseuts, seize and take; and the Quantities of Arms, Ammunition, Provision, and Loading of such Ships, and the true Value of the same, as near as you can judge: And we do hereby jointly charge and command you, as you will answer the same at your utmost Peril, That you do not, in any manner, offend or molest any of our Friends or Allies, their Ships or Subjects, by Colour or Pretence of these Presents, or the Authority hereby granted. In Witness whereof, we have caused our Great Seal of England to be affixed to these Presents. Given at our Court at Kensington, the 26th Day of January 169^, in the Seventh Year of our Reign.

This is a true Copy.

R. Yard.

The said Copy of the Letter from the Lords of the Treasury; viz.

Our very good Lord,

Understanding that One of his Majesty's Men of War is sent, by Order from the Lords Commissioners of the Admiralty here, to bring over Captain Kidd, whom your Lordship hath secured for Piracies in Prison there; we have no Reason to doubt, but that your Lordship's Methods about securing all Treasure and Effects, which are taken and seized as belonging to the said Captain Kidd, or any his Accomplices, or other Pirates, that shall be sent over in the said Ship, from being purloined or embezzled, and sending of the same safe hither, will be effectual: However, we think it our Duty, in respect to his Majesty's Service, to desire, That your Lordship will please to appoint some fit and proper Person to come over with the said Treasure and Effects; and to have particular Care of the same, when on board the said Ship; and that there be several Inventories or Schedules made thereof; One of which we desire your Lordship will please to transmit to us by the first Conveyance that shall offer; and to give another to the Person whom your Lordship shall so think fit to intrust; and a Third to the Captain of the said Man of War; to whom also we desire your Lordship will please to give your Instructions, in case the Person to be appointed by your Lordship shall, in his Passage hither, happen to die. And so we bid you very heartily farewel; and remain,

Our very good Lord,

Y our Lordship's humble Servants,

Cha. Mountague, Treasury Chamber, the J. Smith,

7th of Sept. 1699. H. Boyle.

The said Copy of a Letter about seizing Captain Kidd.

My Lord, Whitehall\ 23 Nov. 1698s

The Lords Justices being informed, by several Ad* vices from the East Indies, of the notorious Piracies committed by Captain Kidd, Commander of the Adventure Gaily; and of his having seized and plundered divers Ships in those Seas; As their Excellencies have given Orders to the Commander of the Squadron fitted out for the East Indies, That he use his utmost Endeavours to pursue and seize the said Kidd, if he continue still in those Parts; so likewise, they have commanded me to signify their Directions to the respective Governors of the Colonies under his Majesty's Obedience in America, That they give strict Orders, and take particular care, for apprehending the said Kidd, and his Accomplices, whenever he or they shall arrive in any of the said Plantations; as likewise, That they secure his Ship, and all the Effects therein: It being their Excellencies Intention, that Right be done to those who have been injured and robbed by the said Kidd; and that he, and his Associates, be prosecuted with the utmost Rigour of the Law: You are to be careful, therefore, duly to observe the said Directions; and, if the said Kidd, or any of his Accomplices, happen to be seized within the Provinces under your Government, you are forthwith to transmit an Account thereof hither; and take care, that the said Persons, Ship, and Effects be secured, till his Majesty's Pleasure be known concerning the m. I am, my Lord,

Your Lordships most

faithful humble Servant,

Ja. Vernon.

A Copy of another Letter to the Secretary of the old East India Company.

Sir, Whitehall, 21th Nov. 1698.

I laid this Day before the Lords Justices*your Letter of the 18th Instant, with the inclosed Advices from India, concerning the Piracies committed by Captain Kidd: Whereupon their Excellencies have ordered, That 12

Instructions be given to the Commander of the Squadron, now going to the East Indies for the Suppressing of the Pirates, That he use his utmost Endeavours to seize the said Kidd, and his Vessel, if he be still in those Seas; in order to the bringing of him, and his Accomplices, to condign Punishment: And their Excellencies have likewise directed, That Instructions be likewise sent to the Earl of Bellomont, for the securing the said Kidd, with his Ship and Associates, in case he return to New York, where the said Kidd hath his Family settled, and from w hence he is said to have carried the greatest1 Part of his Ships Crew; and the like Instructions will be sent to the rest of his Majesty's Colonies in America, that he may be apprehended, whenever he is found, and be proceeded against according to the utmost Rigour of the Law. Their Excellencies finding, by these Advices, how much Captain Wright, the Commander of the Qui-dah Merchant, hath misbehaved himself, in yielding up his Ship to the said Kidd w ithout making any Resistance; and in sharing with him in his Piracies, by taking to his own Use some part of the plundered Goods that belonged to his Freighters; their Excellencies were of Opinion, That the said Wright ought to be apprehended, and made answerable for the same; and they will give Orders for it accordingly, unless the East India Company have any thing to object against it. If there be any thing more that the Company judges proper to be done, on this Occasion, for vindicating the Honour of the Nation against the Calumnies raised in India, and for Security of the Factories there, I desire you will let me know it, that it may be laid before their Excellencies, for their further Directions therein. I am, Sir,

Your most humble Servant,

Ja. Vernon.

A Copy of an Article in the Instructions for the Commanders for Reducing of Pirates in the East Indies. Whereas We have given Orders to the Commanders of our Ships, for the Suppressing of Pirates in the East Indies, to make it their particular Care to pursue and seize the Adventure Gaily, commanded by Captain William Kidd, who, we are informed, has committed divers Piracies in the Seas of India; and, amongst others, has taken a Ship called the Qucdah Merchant, bound from Bengali to Suratt, with Goods to a considerable Value, belonging to the Subjects of the Mogull, and others; Our Will and Pleasure is, in case they meet with and take the said Adventure Gaily, or any of her Prizes, That you secure the said Ship or Ships, with all the Money and Goods found on board the same; and that you cause whatever belongs to any of the Subjects of the Mogull, or any other Merchants in India, to be restored to the right Owners; and that you keep an exact Account of the rest, according to our Pleasure already expressed in these our Instructions: And you are not to make any Promise of Pardon to the said Captain William Kidd, whom We have excepted in our Proclamation.

The Narrative of Captain Thomas South, Commander of the Chamber Frigate, who accompanied the Mogidfs Moca Fleet from Suratt thither, and back again to Suratt.

My sailing Orders and Instructions, given unto me by the General and Council at Bombay, and President and Council at Suratt, were, to proceed along with the Fleet of Ships sailing from Suratt to Moca; and especially to take care, out and home, of the MoguU's owm Ships, wherein were the principal Pilgrims.

Accordingly I sailed thither, leaving Suratt the 22d of March 1697-8. The ldth August following w e departed Moca with 26 Ships in Company and a fair Wind, and got through the Babs the same Night: The next Day had contrary Winds and Calms, and so continued, for the most part, to the 6th of September. These unseasonable Calms, and contrary Winds, made Wood, Water, and all manner of Provisions, so scarce, that some Ships were forced to leave the Fleet, and stand for the Arabian Shore.

The 12th of September a new Ship, about 600 Tons, belonging wholly to the Turks of Judda, commanded by a Ji/rA'called Nocqveda Husson Ammudon, left us, and vias taken by the Pirates the 24th ditto, as we afterw ards heard, in Sight of the Highland of St.Johns. He had 6or 700 People on board, and 26 Horses: Want of Water, made them, as was supposed, desert us.

The 25th of September, in the Afternoon, I saw the Land off St.Johns; and the 30 ditto got safe to an Anchor, with the Mogull's and other Ships in my Company, before Suratt Rivers Mouth; having punctually observed my Orders to the Satisfaction of every body.

London, 22 June, 1699* Tho. South.

Extract of Silratt General Letter to the Easi India Kidd's Company, dated 5th December 1698. Signed by Piracy Samuel Annesley President, Steph. Colt, Ephr. Ben-dali and John Robinson.

' Kidd, in the Adventure Gaily* was riot at the Red Seai nor have we any New's of him where he is; but presume is gone with the Quedah Merchant to Madagascar, or the West Indies to refit and victual, his Ship being very leaky and crazy.

In the beginning of October, Two Pirates of Daman took a Portuguese Ship belonging to that Place, and another of theirs soon after* bound for Dieu; which put us in no small Concern, lest 9ome of the scattered Fleet from the Red Sea should fall into their Hands, as the Gunsway did in the Year 1695* By way of Prevention we proposed, by a Third Person, to the Governor, That he would send for the French Directore, on their Ships the Princess of Savoy and Ponchatrairis Arrival at Bombay, which was the First of September, to order their cruising abroad, to prevent so great an Evil; but to no Purpose.

Next we complained of the Ships exposing themselves to Danger by leaving their Convoy. We were soon convinced our Apprehensions were reasonable, by the unfortunate Seizure of one of the best Ships that belongs to this Port, and the richest that came from Judda. Hei4 Owner is Brother to the Sherreef of that Country: We hear Two Ships took her off the Bar of Daman. The Town, at News of this, was presently in great Disorder*

It was reported the Villains turned adrift in the Ship's Boats, without Oars, Sail, dr Provisions, 150 of the Pilgrims, whom the Tide carried to Bazeen. The Women Passengers^ about Sixty, were kept aboard, and inhumanly abused; to avoid which Indignity Five stabbed themselves. The Treasure, Goods, and Horses, in the Ship, werd computed to be worth 185,000 Rupees.

Upon this, the Governor ordered riorte of our People should be permitted to pass any Gate of the Town; hauled up our Boats to the Custom-house; nor would let any Provisions go to our Ships, which were, through their tedious Passage, in want of all things; and sent hid Officers to the Merchants, to bring their Vessels, thaft were abroad, within the River; and wholly put a Stop to all Proceedings of the Port. Upon this we concluded it necessary to stand upon Guard; and, to that End, and for securing our Countrymen abroad from any Outrage of the Rabble, we called them into the Factory, and sent the Governor word, we designed only to protect ourselves against the Turks and Arabs, that threatened our Lives, and not to oppose the Government; which he consented and advised us to; and we have been ever since, Night and Day, in the same Posture of Defence.

When the Turks, &c. from Baseen, came into the Tow n, some of the principal of them wrote to the Governor for his Permission to revenge themselves upon us: That they would break into the Factory, and rob and murder us, in case he would not do them Justice, as they called it. This he severely forbid them; and threatened, if they should attempt any such thing, he would send his Guards, and cut them off; privately informing us of their Intentions, and his Resolution to defend us.

On the First Council Day afterwards, his House was surrounded with a strong Body of Horse and Foot, to oppose any Tumult the Mob, that were gathering before it, might make; and admitted only to him Two or Three of their Company, telling them He would send up their Complaints to the King, and follow his Orders; and so dismissed them in great Discontent. They combined to draw up a Writing, to be signed by all Mahometans, That the English Infidels had robbed, killed, ductile true Believers; and they would forbear all publick Worship in their Musseets, till the King would order them Satisfaction. But this the Governor, being a stern Man, soon quelled, one by one being afraid to displease him who, they saw, apparently took our Parts.

At present they have, in Conjunction w'ith the Armenians and others, plundered in the Quedah Merchant,

If I had not kept Mr. Secretary Vernon's Orders for seizing and securing Kidd, and his Associates, with all their Effects, with the less Secrecy, 1 had never got him*to comeiu: For his Countrymen, Mr; Graham and Livingston, would have been sure to caution him to shift for himself; and would have been well paid for their Pains.

I received the Lords Justices Orders about Kidd, and likewise Mr. Secretary Vernons, about Three Months before iny leaving New York; but I never discovered them to any body: And, when I heard People say, That the neighbouring (lovemors had Orders from Court to seize him, 1 laughed, as if I believed no such thing. About a Fortnight ago, Bradish and another Pirate got out of Goal of this Town, and escaped, with the Consent of the Gaoler, as there is great Reason to believe.

Eunished with Death: Therefore I desire to receive Were what to do with Bradish's Crew; and also with Kidd, and those Men of his I have taken.

Since my leaving New York, One of the Four Ships has come in that went frotn thence to Madagascar last Summer, and of which I informed your Lordships; and has brought Sixty Pirates, and a vast deal of Treasure.

I hear, that every one of the Pirates paid 150/. for his Passage; and the Owners have, I am told, cleared 30,000l. by this Voyage. It is observable, Mr. Hack-thaw, One of the Merchants that petitioned against me to your Lordships, and Stephen Delaney a hot-headed saucy Frenchman, and Mr. Hackshaws Correspondent, are the thief Owners of this Ship. I hear there are 200 Pirates at Madagascar when this Ship came aw ay, w ho intended to take their Passage in Frederick Phillip's Ship, and the Other Two belonging to New York.

A great Ship has been seen off this Coast many time this Week, supposed to be one Maise, a Pirate, w'ho has brought a vast deal of Wealth from the Red Seas. There is a Sloop also at Rhode Island, which is said to be a Pirate: I hear the Men go ashore there in the Day-time, and return to the Sloop at Night, and spend their Gold very liberally. We can do nothing tow ards the taking those Ships, for Want of a Man of War. I am manning out a Ship to go in quest of the Quedah Metchant left by Kidd on the Coast of Hispaniola: By some Papers which We seized with Kidd, and by his own Confession, we have found out where the Ship lies; and, according to his Account of the Cargo, we compute her to be worth 1o,ooooI. The Ship that carries this is just upon Sailing, and will not be persuaded to stay any longer; so that I cannot send your Lordships the Inventories of the Goods brought in by Kidd, nor the Informations u^e have taken about him from his own Men, till next Opportunity. I am, with respect,

A Copy of a Letter from the Earl of Bellomont to the Council of Trade.

My Lords, Boston, 26th July 99.

I gave your Lordships a short Account of my taking Capt Kidd, in my Letter of the 8th Instant: I shall, in this Letter, confine myself wholly to an Account of my Proceeding with him.

On the 13th of last Month Mr. Emot, a Lawyer of New York, came late at Night to me, and told me he Came from Captain Kidd, who was on the Coast with a Sloop, but would not tell where: That Kidd had brought Sixty Found Weight of Gold, about a hundred Weight of Silver, and Seventeen Bales of East India Goods, which was less by Twenty-four Bales than we have since got in the Sloop: That Kidd had left behind him a great Ship near the Coast of Hispaniola, that nobody but liim-iblfcould find out; ori board whereof there were, in Bale Goods, Saltpetre, and other things, to the Value of at Vol. 13.

least 30,000 /.: That, if I would give hirti Pardon* he Kidd's would bring in the Sloop and Goods hither, and would gcr and fetch the great Ship and Goods afterwards; Air;

Emot delivered me that Night Two French Passes, which Kidd took on board the Two Moors Ships, which were taken by him in the Seas of India, or, as he alleges, by his Men against his Will: One of the Passes wants a Date in the Original, as in the Copy I send your Lordships; and they go N° I. and N° II.

On Thursday, the 1.5th of June, I sent Mr. Campbell, the Post-master of this Town, Kidds Countryman and Acquaintance, along with Mr. Emot, to invite Kidd to comd into this Port: Mr. Campbell returned hither on the 19th of June, and gave in a Memorial to Myself and the Council, containing what had passed between him and Kidd:

The said Memorial goes N° IIL On the said 19th of June, as I sat in Council, I wrote a Letter to Captain Kidd, and shewed it to the Council: and they approving of it*

I dispatched Mr. Campbell again to Kidd with my said Letter; a Copy whereof goes N" IV. Your Lordships may observe, That the Promise I make Captain Kidd, in tny said Letter, of a kind Reception, and promising the King's Pardon for him, is conditional; that is, provided he was as innocent as he pretended to be: But I quickly found sufficient Cause to suspect him very guilty, by the many Lyes and Contradictions he told me. I was so much upon my guard with Kidd, that, he arriving here on Saturday the 8th of this Month, I would not see him, buf before Witnesses; nor have I ever seen him since, but in Council, twice or thrice, that xve examined him; and the Day he was taken up by the Constable, it happened to be by the Door of rnv Lodging, and he rushed in, and came running to me, the Constable after him. I had him not seized till Thursday the 6th Instant; for I had a minds to discover where he had left the great Ship* and I thought myself secure enough from his running away, because I took care not to give him the least Umbrage of my Design of seizing him: Nor had‘I, till that Day that I produced my Orders from Court for apprehending of Kidd, communicated them to any body 2 And I found it necessary to shew tny Orders to the Council, to animate them to join heartily with me in securing Kidd, and examining his Affair nicely, to discover w hat we could of his Behaviour in his whole Voyage* Another Reason w by I took him not up sooner was, that he had brought his Wife and Children hither in the Sloop with him, who, I believed, he would not easily forsake. He being examined twice or thrice by me and the Council, and also some of his Men, 1 observed he seemed much disturbed: And, the last time we examined him, I fancied he looked as if he were upon the Wing, and resolved to run away; and the Gentlemen of the Council had some of them the same thought with mine, so that I took their Consent in seizing and committing him: But the Officers appointed to seize his Men were so careless, as to let T hree or Four of his Men escape; which troubled me the more, because they were old New York Pirates.

The next thing the Council and I did w as to appoint a Committee of trusty Persons, to search for the Goods and Treasure brought by Kidd; and to secure what they should find, till the Kings Pleasure should he known as to the Disposition thereof, as my Orders from Air. Secretary Vernon import. The said Committee were made up of Two Gentlemen of the Council, Two Merchants, and the Deputy Collector, whose Names are to the inclosed Inventory of the Goods and Treasure. They searched Kidd's Lodgings, and found hid and made up in Two Sea Beds, a Bag of Gold Dust and Ingots, of the Value of about 1,000l.; and a Bag of Silver, part Money, and part Pieces and Pigs of Silver, Value asset down in the said Inventory. In the above Bag of Gold were several little Bags of Gold: All Particulars are very justly and exactly set down in the Inventory, I believe.

For my Part, I have meddled with no manner of thing; but put every thing under the Management of the Council, and into the Custody of the before-mentioned Committee

mittee, that 1 might be free from the Suspicion and Censure of the World.

The enamelled Box, mentioned in the Beginning of the Inventory, is that which Kidd made a Present of to my Wife by Mr. Campbell-, which 1 delivered in Council to

the said Committee, to keep with the rest of the Treasure. There was in it a Stone Bing, which we take to be a

BristollSione: If it were true, it would be worth about 40/.: And there was a small Stone unset, which we believe is also counterfeit; and a Sort of a Locket, with Four Sparks, which seem to be right Diamonds; for there is nobody here that understands Jewels. If the Box, and all that is in it, were right, they cannot be worth above 6°/.

Your Lordships will see, in the middle of the Inventory, a Parcel of Treasure and Jewels, delivered up by Mr. Gardiner of Gardiner's Island in the Province of Next) York, and at the East End of Nassau Island; the Recovering and Seizing of which Treasure is owing to my own Care and Quickness. I heard, by greatest Accident in the World, the Day that Captain Kidd was committed, That a Man had offered 30/. for a Sloop to carry him to Gardiners Island; and Kidd having owned he had borrowed some Gold on that Island, though he never mentioned to us any Jewels, nor, I believe, would he have owned the Gold there, but that he thought he should be sent for it, I presently reflected, that That Man, whom I have since discovered to be one of s Men, was to defeat us of that Treasure: I privately posted away a Messenger by Land, with a peremptory Order to Mr. Gardiner, in the King's Name, to come forthwith,

and deliver up such Treasure as or any of his Crew', had lodged with him; acquainting him, That I had committed Kidd to Gaol, as I was ordered to do by the King. My Messenger made great Haste, and was with Gardiner before any body; and Gardiner, who is a very substantial Man, brought away the Treasure without Delay, and, by my Direction, delivered it into the Hands of the Committee. If the Jewels be right, as it is supposed they are, but I never saw them, nor the Gold and Silver brought by Gardiner, then we guess that the Parcel brought by him may be worth, Gold, Silver, and Jewels, 4,500l.; And besides, Kidd had left six Bales of Goods with him, One of which was tw ice as big as any of the rest; and Kidd gave him a particular Charge of that Bale, and told him, it was worth 2,000 /.: The Six Bales Gardiner could not bring; but 1 have ordered him to send them by a Sloop that is since gone from hence to Nexc York, which is to return speedily. We are not able to set an exact Value on the Goods and Treasure we have got, because we have not opened the Bales we took on board the Sloop: But we hope, when the Six Bales are sent in by Gardiner, what will be then in the Hands of the Gentlemen appointed to that Trust, will amount to about 14,000l. I have sent strict Orders to my Lieutenant Governor at New York, to make diligent Search for the Goods and Treasure sent by Kidd to New York, in Three Sloops mentioned in Gardiner's Affidavit, which I send, with the other Affidavits and Informations, to your Lordships; and I believe I have directed him where to find a Purchase in a House at New York, which, by a Hint I have had, I am apt to believe will be found out in that House. 1 have sent to search elsewhere a certain Place strongly suspected to have received another Deposition of Gold from Kidd. I am also upon the Hunt for Two or Three Arch Pirates, which I hope to give your Lordships a good Account of by my next Conveyance. If I could have but a good able Judge and Attorney General at York,a Man of War there, and another here, and the Companies recruited and well paid, I will rout Pirates and Piracy intirely out of all this North Part of America: But, as I have too often told your Lordships, it is impossible for me to do all this alone in my single Person.

I wrote your lordships Word, in my last Letter of the 8th Instant, That Bradish the Pirate, and One of his Crew, were escaped out of the Gaol of this Tow n. We

have since found, that the Gaoler was ' Kinsman;

and the Gaoler confessed, they went out at the Prison Door, and that he found it wide open. We had all the Reason in the World to believe the Gaoler was consenting to the Escape: By much ado I could get the Council to resent the Gaoler's Behaviour; but, by mere Importunity, I had the fellow before us: We examined him, and, by his own Story, and Accounts given us of his suffering other Prisoners formerly to escape, I prevailed to have him turned out, and a Prosecution ordered against him to the Attorney General. I have also, with some Difficulty, this late Session of Assembly here, got a Bill to pass, That the Gaol be committed to the Care of the High Sheriff of the County, as in England, with a Salary of 30/. per Annum, to the said Sheriff: I w'ould have had it 50/. per Annum, for the Sheriff's Encouragement to be honest and careful; but I could not prevail. I am forced to allow the Sheriff 405. per IVfor keeping Kidd safe, otherwise I should be in some Doubt about him. He has, without Doubt, a great deal of Gold, which is apt to tempt Men that have not Principles of Honour:

I have therefore, to try the Power of dull Iron against Gold, put him into Irons that weigh Sixteen Pound Weight. I thought it moderate enough; for I remember, poor Doctor Oates had a Hundred Weight of Iron on him, when he was a Prisoner in the late Reign. There never was a greater Lyar in the World than this Kidd:notwithstanding he assured the Council and me, every time we examined him, That the great Ship, and her Cargo, waited his Return to bring her hither; and now your Lordships will see, by Two several Informations of Masters of Ships from , that the Cargo

has been sold there: And, in-One of them, it is said, they have burnt that noble Ship; and, without Doubt, it was by Kidds Order, that the Ship might not be an Evidence against him; for he would not ow n to us her Name was the Qucdah Merchant, though his Men did. Andries Henlyne, and Two more, brought the first News to New York, of the Sale of that Cargo at Curacoa; and never such Pennyworths heard of for Cheapness. Captain Exxrtz is he w ho has brought the New s of the Ship's being burnt. She was of about 500 Ton; and Kidd told us at the Council, there never was a stronger or stauncher Ship seen. His Lying had like to have involved me in a Contract, that would have been very chargeable, and to no manner of Purpose, as he has ordered Matters. I was advised by Council to dispatch a Ship of good Countenance, to go and fetch away that Ship and Cargo.

I had agreed for a Ship of 300 Tons, 22 Guns; and I was to man her with Sixty Men, to force, if there had been need of it, the Men to yield who were left with the Ship. I w as just going to seal the Writing, when I bethought myself it were best to press Kidd, once more to tell me Truth. I therefore sent to him Two Gentlemen of the Council to the Gaol; and he at last owned, That he had left a Power with one Mr. j , a

Merchant of Antegoa, w hom he had committed the Care

of the Ship to, to sell and dispose of all the Cargo: Upon which Confession of Kidd's I held my Hand from hiring that great Ship, which would have cost 1,700l. by Computation. And now Tomorrow I send the Sloop Captain Kidd came in, with the Letters to the Lieutenant Governor of Antegoa, Colonel Yeomans, to the Governors

of St. Thomas's Island and- Curacoa, to seize and secure w hat Effects they can, that was late in the Possession of Kidd, and on board the Qucdah Merchant. There is one Burt, an Englishmen, that lives at St. Thomas, who has got a great Store of the Goods and Money for Kidd's Account. St. Thomas belongs to the Danes; but I hope to retrieve what Burt has in his Hands. The sending this Sloop will cost but about 300l. if she be out Three Months. I hope your Lordships will take care, that immediate Orders be sent to Antegoa to secure Bolton, w ho must have played the Knave egregiously; for he could not but know', that K came knavishly by that Sloop and Goods. Since my Commitment of Kidd, I hear, That, upon his Approach to this Port, his Heart misgave him; and he proposed to his Men, the putting to Sea again, and going to Caledonia, the new Scotch Settlement, near Darien;

but they refused.

I desire I may have Orders what to do with and all his and Bradish' Crew; for as the Law stands in this Country, if a Pirate were convict, yet he cannot suffer Death: And the Council here refused to pass the Bill to punish Privateers and Pirates, which your Lordships sent with me from England, with a Direction to recommend

it at New York and here, to be passed into a Law. I shall, by next Conveyance, acquaint your Lordships, what a Prejudice I have found in some of the Council to the J^aws of England this Session; but, having writ myself almost dead, I must, till another Opportunity, forbear to treat of the Affairs of this. Province; but, when I do, I must tell your Lordships beforehand, I will not dissemble with you, to favour any Man, or Number of Men; I am both above it, and I should think I did not do the Part of an honest Man, if I concealed any thing from you, that tends to the Prejudice of the Interest of England.

You will observe, by some of the Informations I now send, That Kidd did not only rob the Two Moors Ships, but also a Portuguese Ship; which he denied absolutely to the Council and me.

I send your Lordships Twenty-four several Papers and Evidences relating to Captain Kidd: It is impossible for me to animadvert, and make Remarks, on the several Matters contained in the said Papers, in the weak Condition I am at present; but must leave that Trouble to Mr. Secretary Popple, whose excellent clear Method in Business fits him incomparably beyond me for such a Work.

I will always continue to be, with much Respect,

My Lords,

Your Lordships most humble

and obedient Servant*

Bellomont,

N® III. The Memorial of Duncan Campbell, of Boston, humbly presented to his Excellency the Earl of

Bellomont.

I, the said Duncan Campbell, being at Rhode Island on Saturday the 17th June current; that Morning I went iu a Sloop from the said Island, in Company with Mr. Janies Emott of New York, and Two other Men belonging to the said Sloop, towards Block Islaand, about Three Leagues from that Island, I met a Sloop commanded by Captain Kidd, and having on board about Sixteen Mert

besides; after hailing of which Sloop, and being informed,

That the said Kidd was Commander thereof, he the said Kidd desired me to come on board the same; which I accordingly did, and, after some Discourse passed, the said Kidd desired me to do him the Favour as to make what Speed I could for Boston, and acquaint your Excellency,-That the said Kidd had brought a Ship, about 5 or 690 Tons, from Madagascar, which, some considerable time since, he met within* and commanded her there to bring to; and that thereupon the Pilot, being a,

came on board the said Kidd's Ship, and told him, the said Kidd, He was welcome, and that the said Ship, to which the said Pilot belonged, was a lawful Prize to him, the said Kidd, she sailing under & French Pass: Whereupon he, the said Kidd, and Company, took the said Ship; and afterwards, understanding that the same belonged to the Moors, he, the said Kidd, would have delivered her up again; but his Men violently tell upon him, and thrust him into his Cabin, saying, The said Ship was a fair Prize; and then carried her into Madagascar, and rifled her of what they pleased: But before they got into Madagascar, the Gaily under Command of him, the said Kidd, became so leaky, that she would scarce keep above Water; whereupon the Company belonging thereto, having taken out her Guns, and some other Things, and put them on board the Prize, set the said Gaily on Fire.

The said Captain Kidd further told me, That, when he and his Company were arrived at Madagascar, several of his Company moved him to go and take a Ship called the Moco Frigate, that lay ready fitted at a Place not far distant from them, in the Possession of certain Privateers; and to go in the same for the Red Sea; but that he the said Kidd said, That, if they would join with him, he would attempt the taking of the said Ship, supposing her a lawful Prize, being formerly belonging to the King of England; but would not afterwardsgo with them on the said Design to the Red Sea: Whereupon Ninety of his, the said Kidd's Men, deserted him, went and took the said G Ship

Ship, and sailed with the same on the said Design, as he, the said Kidd, was informed; obligingone Captain Culliver, the then Commander of her, to go along with them.

And the said Kidd further told me, That his Men having left him, and his Design frustrated, he thought it his best Way to preserve the said Ship then in his Possession, and the Goods on board her, for his Employers, or the proper Owners thereof: And accordingly, with the few Men lie had then left, which w ould not join with the other Ninety in their aforesaid Design, beingaboirt Twenty in Number, and with a few other Men, that he procured at Madagascar, to assist him in navigating the said Ship, he intended to have brought the same to Boston, according to his Orders; but, touching in his Way at the Island of St. Thomas, and other Places in the West Indies, he there heard, That great Complaints were preferred against him, and lie proclaimed a Pirate; which occasioned him to sail to a Place called Mona, near Hispaniola; from whence he sent to Curaso, and bought there (he Sloop on which he is now on board, and took into her to the Value of about 8 or ?0,000 L in Goods, Gold, and Plate; for which Gold and Plate he traded at Madagascar, and was produced by the Sale of sundry Goods and Stores, that he took out of the Adventure Gaily, formerly commanded by him; and hath left the Ship taken by his Company, and carried to Madagascar, as aforesaid, at or near Mona abovesaid, in the Custody of about Six Men of his own Company, and Eighteen others that he got from Curaso; the Merchant, of whom he bought the said Sloop, being intrusted therewith; unto which he hath promised to return again in Three Months; the said Kidd resolving to come into Boston, or New York, to deliver up unto your Excellency what Goods and Treasure he hath on board; and to pray your Excellency's Assistance, to enable him to bring the said Ship, left by him at Mom aforesaid, from thence; the said Ship being disabled from coming for want of Furniture.

But the said Captain Kidd further informed me, That by reason of what his Men had heard in the West Indies, as aforesaid, of their being proclaimed Pirates, they would not consent to his coming into any Port without some Assurance from your Excellency, That they should not be imprisoned nor molested: And the said Captain Kidd did several times protest solemnly, That he had not done any thing since his going out in the said Gaily contrary to his Commission and Orders, more than what he was necessitated unto, being overpowered by his Men that deserted him, as aforesaid; who evil-intreated him several times for his not consenting to, or joining with them in, their Actions: And all the Men on board the Sloop now with hhn did, in like manner, solemnly protest their Innocence; and declared, That they had used their utmost Endeavours in preserving the aforesaid Ship and Goods for the Owners or Employers.

The said Kidd also said, That, if your Lordship should see Cause so to direct, he would carry the said Ship for England\ there to render an Account of his Proceedings.

N* IV. A Copy of the Earl of Bdlomont's Letter lo Captain Kidd.

Captain, Kidd, Boston, 19 June 1699.

Mr. Emott came to me last Tuesday Night late, telling me, He came from you, but was shy of telling where he parted with you; nor did I press him to it: He told me, You came to Oyster Bay, in Nassaio Island, and sent for him to New York. He proposed to me, That I would grant you a Pardon: I answered, That I had never granted one yet; and that I had set myself a Rule, not to grant a Pardon to any Body whatever without the King's express Leave or Command: He told me, You declared and protested your Innocence; and that, if your Men could be persuaded to follow* your Example, you would make no Manner of Scruple of coming into this

Port, or any other within his Majesty's Dominions: That you owned there were Two Ships taken; but that your Men did it violently, against your Will; and had used you barbarously, in imprisoning you, and treating you ill, most Part of the Voyage, and often attempting to murder you. Mr. Emott delivered me Twto French Passes, taken on board the Two Ships which your Men rifled; which Passes I have in my Custody; and I am apt to believe they will be a good Article to justify you, if the late Peace were not, by the Treaty between England and France, to operate in that Part of the World at the time the Hostility was committed, as I am almost confident it was not to do. Mr. Emott also told me, You had to about the Value of 10,000l. in the Sloop with you; and that you had left a Ship somewhere off the Coast of Hispaniola, in which there was to the Value of 30,000l. more, which you had left in safe Hands, and had promised to go to your People in that Ship, within Three Months, to fetch them with you to a safe Harbour. These are all the material Particulars I can recollect that passed betw een Mr. Emott and me: Only this, that he told me, that you shewed a great Sense of Honour and Justice, in professing, with many Asseverations, your settled and serious Design, all along, to do Honour to your Commission, and never to do the least Thing contrary to your Duty and Allegiance to the King: And this I have to say in your Defence, That several Persons at New York, who I can bring to evidence it, if there be Occasion, did tell me, That by several Advices from Madagascar, and that Part of the World, they were informed of your Men's revolting from you in one Place; which I am pretty sure they said was at Madagascar; and that others of them compelled you, much against your Will, to take and rifle Two Ships.

I have advised with his Majesty's Council, and shewed them this Letter, this Afternoon; and they are of Opinion, That if your Case be so clear as you (or Mr. Emott for you) have said, then you may safely come hither, and be equipped, and fitted out, to go and fetch the other Ship; and I make no Manner of Doubt but to obtain the King's Pardon for you, and those few Men you have left; who, I understand, have been faithful to you, and refused, as well as you, to dishonour the Commission you had from England.

I assure you, on my Word and Honour, I will perform nicely what I have now promised: Tliough this I declare beforehand, That whatever Treasure or Goods you bring hither, I will not meddle with the least Bit of them; but they shall be left with such trusty Persons as the Council shall advise, until I receive Orders from England, how they shall be disposed of.

Mr. Campbell will satisfy you, That this, That I have now writ, is the Sense of the Council, and of

Your humble Servant. Boston, June the 19th, 1699.

His Excellency read this Letter in Council: Which was approved of by them.

Isa. Addington, Secretary.

N* V. A Copy of Captain Kidd's Letter to the Earl of BeUommt.

From Block Island Road, on board the Sloop St Antonio, June the 24th, 1699.

May it please your Excellency,

I am honoured with your Lordship's kind Letter of the 19th current, by Mr. Campbell; which came to my Hands this Day; for which I return my most hearty Thanks.

I cannot but blame myself for not writing to your Lordship before this Time, knowing it was my Duty; but the Clamours, and false Stories, that have been reported of me, made me fearful of writing, or coming into any Harbour, till I could hear from your Lordship.

I note the Contents of your Lordship's Letter: As to what Mr. Emott and Mr. Campbell informed your Lordship of my Proceedings, I do affirm to be true; and a great Deal more might be said of the Abuses of my Men, and the Hardship I have undergone to preserve the Ship,

and

n

and what Goods my Men had left: Ninety-five T\Ien went away from me in one Day, and went on board the Moca Frigate, Captain Robert Cullifar Commander; who went away to the Red Seas; and committed several Acts of Piracy, as I am informed; and am afraid (the Men formerly belonging to myXJally) that the Report is gone Homeugainst me to the East India Company, That I have been the Actor: A Sheet of Paper will not contain what may be said of the Care I took to preserve the Owners Interest, and to come Home to clear my own Innocency. I do further declare and protest, That I never did, in the least, act contrary to the King's Commission, nor to the Reputation of my honourable Owners; and doubt not but I shall be able to make my Innocence appear; or else I had no need to come to these Parts of the World, if it wefe not for that, and my Owners Interest There are Five or Six Passengers, that came from Mallegasco to assist me in bringing the Ship Home, and about Ten of my own Men, that came with me, would not venture to

Erato Boston, till Mr. Campbell had engaged, Body for dv, for them, That they should not be molested while Istaid at Boston, or till I return with the Ship. I doubt not but your Lordship will write to England in my favour, and for these few Men, that are left. I wish your Lordship would persuade Mr. Campbell to go Home for England, with your Lordship s Letters: Who w ill be able to give Account of our Affairs, and diligently follow the same, that there may he a speedy Answer from England.

I desired Mr. Campbell to buy 1,000 Weight cf Rigging, for fitting of the Ship to bring her to Boston, that I may not be delayed, when I come there. LIpon receiving of your Lordship's Letter, I am making the best of my Way for Boston.

This, with my humble Duty to your Lordship and Countess, is what offers from, my Lord,

Your Excellency's most humble and dutiful Servant,

Wm. Kidd.

Boston'm New-England, 8 July 1699.

Mr. Gardiner,

' Having received the King's express Orders for seizing and securing the Bodies of Captain Kiddy.. all his Associates, together with all their Effects, and till I should receive his Majesty's Royal Pleasure how to dispose of the same; I have accordingly secured Captain Kidd in the Gaol of this Town, and some of his Men: He has been examined by myself, and the Council, and has confessed, among other Things, That he left with you. a Parcel of Gold, made up in a Box, and some other Parcels besides; All which I require you, in his Majesty's Name, immediately to bring hither to me, that 1 may secure them for his Majesty's (Jse; and I shall recompense your Pains in coming hither. That, in the Month of May last, he was at Curacoa; and, after he had been there Three or Four Weeks, News arrived, That Captain Kidd, with his Ship, was at the Island of Savona, to the South-east of Hispaniola;

from thence.....was brought by a Curacoa Master to

the Island St. Helena, nigh Hispaniola; where the same was brought in a Salt-Lagon; where the Inhabitants of Curacoa and St. Thomas traded with the same, and carried off several Sloops Load: And the said Evertz has seen some of the Goods brought to Curacoa: Whereupon the said Evertz did address himself to the Governor of Curacoa, Bostiaen Bernage, desiring his Assistance to hinder such a wicked Trade, seeing it was unlawful to trade with Pirates: All which, by some Accidents, was hindered, $c. And the said Evertz, departing from Curacoa, bound to this Port of New York; and, by reason of the Northerly Wind, not being able to reach above St. Helena, where the said Ship of Captain Kidds lay in the aforesaid Lagon, and was almost burnt down; which was on the 29th of June last, when the said Evertz saw it on Fire; there being then Two Sloops at that Place.

N° XI. A Copy of the Narrative of JVrri. Cuthbert, late Gunner of the Ship Charles the 2d, Captain John Dorrcll Commander, of 60 Guns and Two Mortar Pieces, is as followeth: From the Lat. 27 Deg. f. Delivered the 8th of July 1699.

That, coming out of the Gulf of Persia, in the Latitude of 22 Degrees and 30 Minutes North Lat. we saw a Ship to Windward of us; which bore down upon us, and stood athwart our Forefoot, and came within Gunshot of us: Upon which, I was commanded by our said Captain to place a Shot betwixt her Forefoot; and, upon the same, he clapt his Helm hard-a-weather, and bore away right before it: Whereupon we concluded it to be Captain Kidd, of whom we had heard, That he was in that Latitude; at which time, we judged ourselves Sixty Leagues distant from the Land: And, about Four Days after, we came to an Anchor at Bombay; where the General of all those Parts of the Indies, and William Burnister, who is the Second in Command, satisfied our Commander, That the Ship aforesaid which we saw was Kidd; and said. That, the other Day, the said Kidd was in Curzvarr, one of the East India Company Factories, and watered there; at which time Two of Kidd's Men left him, because, as they said, he was going upon an ill Design of Piracy: Upon which the said Men were secured by the Chief in Command, named Upton, till they could be sent to the General at Bombay; who afterwards sent them on board our Ship, Captain Dorrcll Commander, then bound for England, wrhich was on Saturday the 29th January 1697, as Prisoners, to be examined before the Admiralty in England: Which was done: Who wrere found innocent, in that they had left Kiddm time, before he had committed Piracy; and so the said Men were cleared: But, before we went from Bombay, our said Captain was informed by the General, That the said JV/7/r/had taken a great Ship of the Bantams, and also took and kept the Mate of her, which was an Englishmen: Upon which Depredations, it is usual for the Inhabitants of those Countries to take the English there, and secure them, and seize upon their Estates for Satisfaction; which if wanting, many Families, Men, Women, and Children, have perished in Prison: And, as we went home for England, with the said Two Men, that left Kidd, they told us, That he had made many Attempts upon Vessels, but could not prevail; and that he was very cruel to his Men, and abused them, especially such as did not adhere to those evil Practices; which was the Cause that they had left him, as aforesaid.

And further he saith, That as soon as we came with our said Captain Dorrell, with the said Ship upon those Coasts, which was *, We heard, That one Captain Edg-comb, Commander of a Ship belonging to the Company, called the Moquo Frigate, about 3bo Tons, w as murdered by his Men, as he lay asleep on his Couch on board his Ship; and, it w^as reported, That it w as one Gillam, that had turned Moor, and was circumcised, who was shipt on board the said Edgcomb, and One of those Twelve Men, whose Names are hereafter mentioned, who ran away with the said Moquo Frigate, after they had killed the said Captain Edgcomb; which said Gillam went by the Name of Sampson Marshall in the Indies.

The Names of the said Men are, Sampson Marshall alias Gillam, Thomas Preston, Ralph Stout, Thomas Alcock, John Swan, Martin Neales, John Perncll, Joseph Pell, Richard Sims, William Burrell, Christian Peterson, Thomas Stevens.

Moreover, when we came homeward-bound, about the , to the Cape Bon Espc ranee, we were informed by a Dutchman, That the Moquo Frigate, after she wras run away with, hoarded one Captain Mine, in the Ship Dorrell, which did properly belong to Our Captain Dorrell, and his Father in London, who had been in the Company s Service; but he blew them up, killed and wounded many of their Men, so that they were forced to leave him: But he, being much disabled by those Pirates, was fain to put into an Island called Jabbce to recruit; and so went for Bombay, to rebuild the Wastes of his Ship; and so for England, being the re expected last March. Now, whether there be any of the above-named Men come into these Parts with Captain Kidd, as wrell as this Gillam at Rhode Island, w ho is vehemently to be suspected to be one, is to me unknown; but may be inquired into.

By me Wm. Cuthbert.

A true Copy. BellomonL

That he being Master of the said Sloop Antonio, lately belonging to Antony Montero, Abraham Redwood, and Henry Boulton, of Antegoa, Merchants, and in their Employ on a Voyage from Antegoa to Curacoa and Royaldc Hatch, the said Boulton Supra-cargo, and returning from Royal De Hatch to Curacoa, they there took in a small Quantity of Goods to trade for Hogs at Port Rieco, to carry with them to Antegoa; and sailed from Curacoa towards Port Rieco; and, off the West End of the said Island of Port Rieco, they espied a large Ship: Some of the Company belonging to said Ship came, in a Canoe, on board the said Sloop; and desired the Examinant to stand for the said Ship, and to supply them with some Provisions: And, the said Sloop being then near to the Shore, the Examinant stood in to the same with his said Sloop, and took in betwixt 30 and 40 Hogs, and put them into the Ships Boat, which afterwards came to the said Sloop, and sent them on board in her; Mr. Boulton his Supra-cargo going in the Boat before them: The Men that came on board the Sloop from the Ship informed. N° XIIL The Examination of Thortias Way, of Boston, Mariner.

Saith,

That, coming lately from the Bay of Compeach, in the Sloop whereof he is Commander, upon the Shoals of Nantucket on Friday the 30th of June last, the Sloop whereof Captain Kidd was Commander, came up with him; and they hailed each other; and, being both bound in for Boston, sailed together in Company: And the Examinant, in his Canoe, with Two of his Ship's Company, went on board the said Captain Kidd's Sloop; and Captain Kidd presented the Examinant with a Bit of a Bar of Gold; and, at his coining off again from the said Sloop, by Order of Captain Kidd, there was put into the Examinants Canoe, Three Fire Arms, a Pair of Stilliards, a Turkey Carpet, a Clock, and a small Bundle, made up in a Napkin, or a Piece of Ossnabriggs, loosely fastened together; which, the said Kidd told the Examinant, was some of his Wife's Cloaths, and desired him to carry up for him; which he accordingly did: And Mrs. ZGWsentfor the said Bundle, soon after their coming to Boston; which was delivered: The Clock, Carpet, and Stilliards, remain at the Examinants House; the Arms are at the Gunsmiths: There was also delivered unto the Examinant,'by the said Kidd, a Bag of coarse Canvas, sealed up (the Bag had Two Seals) about the Bigness of the Crown of his Hat; which, he said, contained Reals of Eight, that his Wife brought with her from New York to bear her Expences: And the Morning of the same Day that Captain Kidd was taken, he came to the Examinant's House with a Negro Boy, and fetched away the said Bag of Money: He judges it might weigh Six Pound Weight:

There was Eight Pound more, in Pieces of Eight Reals, and Arabian Gold, delivered unto this Examinant by

Aires, One of the said Kidd's Company, to secure for him; and, this Morning, the said Aires sent a written Order, from the Prison, unto the Examinant, to deliver his Money to George Riscarrick; which he accordingly did, only Ten or a Dozen Double Reals still resting in the Examinant's Hand: His Piece of Gold he sold to Mr. Dummer, for 41, odd Money. Thomas Way.

N°XVII. A Copy of the Examination of Hugh Parrott, of Plymouth in the County of Devo?i, Mariner,

Who saith, That at the Island of Joanna, he left the Vessel he then belonged to, and entered himself on board the Adventure Gaily, Captain William Kidd Commander; and from thence we sailed to the Red Sea, and there cruised for Privateers and Pirates; but finding none, went upon the Coast of India, and, in our Cruise there, espied a Ship, which we gave Chace to, and came up with, being a Ship of near 200 Tons Burden, whereof a Dutchman, Mich. Dicker, was Master; and there w ere Two more Dutchmen on board; all the rest of the Company were Moors, being about Forty in Number in the Whole; and the said DutchMaster, being commanded on board the Gaily, brought a French Pass, and, as the Examinant was informed, declared, That his Ship and Lading was lawful Prize; and accordingly was made Prize of by the said Kidd and Company: The Dutch Master remained in the Gaily with the other Two Dutchmen, and took up Arms to serve under Captain Kidd; the Moors were set on Shore, being then not above Two Leagues distant from the same: The Examinant knows not what the Ship was laden with; only saw Two Horses sent on Shore from her. And in about Six Weeks Time afterward, they took another Ship of 400 Tons, or upwards, mounted with about 12 or 14 Guns, commanded by one Captain/FngAf, an Englishmen; and there was also on board Two or Three Dutchmen; the rest of the Company were Armenians and Moors, to the Number of about Sixty or Seventy: The Ship came from Bengali, bound to Per-tia, as it was said; and that she belonged wholly to the Moors: She was laden with Bale Goods, containing Muslins, Silk striped and plain, and raw Silk, refined Sugar in Bags, Saltpetre, Iron in Junks, Guns, and Anchors: Captain fVright and other the Christians, with several of the Armenians and Moors, were speedily sent on Shore; some of them came to Madagascar in the Gaily, and there left her: Said, Captain Kidd carried the said Prize Ship into Madagascar, Geo. Bullen, Chief Mate of the Gaily, being put in to command the said Prize Ship; and when she arrived at Madagascar, they took out of her all the Bale Goods, and shared them among the Gally's Company, being about One hundred in Number, more or less; some had Three, others Four Bales to a Share; the Examinant had Four for his Share, which he sold at Hispaniola, to Mr. Boulton and Mr. Burt, for 400 Pieces of Eight, which was paid him down in Money; 200 Pieces of which he lost since by Gaming, on board the Sloop Antonio, that he came from Hispaniola in; the rest of his Money was stolen from him. N0 XIX. A Copy of the Narrative of John Gardner of Gardner's Island, alias IsleofJVight, relating to Captain William Kidd.

That, about Twenty Days ago, Mr. Emot of New York came to the Narrator's House, and desired a Boat to go for New York; telling the Narrator he came from my Lord at Boston: Whereupon the Narrator furnished the said Emot with a Boat; and he went for New York: And that Evening the Narrator saw a Sloop with Six Guns riding at an Anchor off Gardners Island: And Two Days afterwards, in the Evening, the Narrator went aboard the said Sloop to inquire what she was; and, so soon as he came on board, Captain Kidd\ then unknown to the Narrator, asked him how himself and Family did; telling him. That he, the said Kidd, w>as going to my Lord at Boston; and desired the Narrator to take Three Negroes, Two Boys and a Girl, ashore, to keep till he, the said Kidd, or his Order, should call for them; which the Narrator accordingly did: That, about Two Hours after the Narrator had got the said Negroes ashore, Captain Kidd sent his Boat ashore with Two Bales of Goods and a Negro Boy: And the Morning after, the said Kidd desired the Narrator to come immediately on board, and bring Six Sheep with him, for his the said Kidd's Voyage to Boston; which the Narrator did; when Kidd asked him to spare a Barrel of Cyder; which the Narrator, with great Importunity, consented to; and sent Two of his Men for it, who brought the Cyder on board the said Sloop: But whilst the Men w ere gone for the Cyder, Captain Kidd offered the Narrator several Pieces of damnified Muslins and Bengals, as a Present to his Wife; which the said Kidd put in a Bag, and gave the Narrator; and about a Quarter of an Hour afterwards, the said Kidd took up Two or Three Pieces of damnified Muslin, and gave the Narrator for his proper Use: And the Narrators Men then coming on board with the said Barrel of Cyder, as aforesaid, the said Kidd gave them Four Pieces 01 Arabian Gold for their Trouble and also for bringing him Wood: Then the said Kidd, ready to sail, told this'Narrator he would pay for his Cyder; to which the Narrator answered, That he was already satisfied for it by the Present to his Wife. And this Narrator observed, That some of KidcTs Men gave to the Narrator's Men some inconsiderable Things of small Value, which, this Narrator believes, were Muslins for Neckcloths: And then the Narrator took Leave of the said Kidd, and went ashore; and, at parting, the said ISudd fired Four Guns, and stood for Block Island.

About Three Days afterwards, the said Kidd sent the Master of the Sloop and one Clark, in his Boat, for the Narrator, who went on board with them: And the said Kidd desired this Narrator to take on Shore with him, and keep for him, the said Kidd, and Order, a Chest, and a Box of Gold, and a Bundle of Quilts, and Four Bales of Goods; which Box of Gold, the said Kidd told the Narrator, was intended for my Lord; and the Narrator complied with the said Kidd's Request, and took on Shore the said Chest, Box of Gold, Quilts, and Bales of Goods.

And the Narrator further saith, That Two of Kidd's Crew, who went by the Names of Cook and Pam at, delivered to him, the Narrator *Two Bags of Silver; which, they told the Narrator, weighed Thirty Pound Weight; for which he gave Receipt: And that another of Kidd's Men delivered to the Narrator a small Bundle of Gold, and Gold Dust, of about a Pound Weight, to keep for him; and did also present the Narrator with a Sash, and a Pair of Worsted Stockings: And just before the Sloop sailed, Captain Kidd presented the Narrator with a Bag of Sugar; and then took Leave, and sailed for Boston.

And the Narrator further saith, He knew nothing of Kidd's being proclaimed a Pirate; and if he had, he durst not have acted otherwise than he has done, having no Force to oppose them; and for that he hath formerly been threatened to be killed by Privateers, if he should carry unkindly to them. John Gardiner.

The within-named Narrator further saith, That whilst Captain Kidd lay with his Sloop at Gardner's Island, there was a New York Sloop, whereof one Coster is Master and his Mate is a little black Man, unknown to the Narrator by Name* who, as it was said, had been formerly Captain Kidd's Quarter-master; and another Sloop belonging to New York, Jacob Fenick Master; both which lay near to Kidd's Sloop Three Days together: And whilst the Narrator was on board with Captain Kidd, there w as several Bales of Goods, and other Things, put out of the said Kidd's Sloop, and put on board the other Two Sloops aforesaid; and the said Two Sloops sailed up the Sound: After which Kidd sailed with his Sloop for Block Island; and being absent for the Space of Three Days, returned to Gardners Island again, in Company of another Sloop belonging to Nexv York, Cornelius Quick Master; on board of which was one Thomas Clark of Setanket, commonly called JVhisking Clark, and ope Harrison of Jamaica, Father to a Boy that was with Captain Kidd; and Captain Kidd's Wife was then on board his own Sloop: And Quick remained with his Sloop there from Noon till the Evening of the same Day, and took on board Two Chests, that came out of the said Kidd's Sloop* under the Observance of this Narrator; and, he believes,
