The Translation of the Treaty of Altena.

B E it known to all, by what means the great Controversies, which have been a long time between his Royal Majesty of Denmark, and Norway, and his Highness the Duke of Holstein Sleswick, by the earnest Mediation of his Imperial Majesty, and their Electoral Highnesses of Saxony and Brandenburgh, nave been composed, and forever abolished, upon the following Conditions:

1. That there shall be a General Amnesty, and a perpetual Oblivion, of all that hath been hitherto undertaken on both Sides, done or acted by each, or other Party, their Ministers, Subjects, or Adherents; none of either Side shall be called to an Account, nor shall any body be brought into Danger or Charge for it: But an eternal and indissolvable Friendship and Union shall hereby be restored and established betwixt his Royal Majesty of Denmark and Nunvay, his Heirs and Successors, in his Kingdoms, and his Highness the Duke of Holstein Sles-xvicky and his Successors.

2. His Royal Majesty of Denmark and Norway shall restore to his Ducal Highness all his said Highness's Dominions, Lands, Islands, and Goods; but especially the Lordship of Gottesgabe, together with the Sovereign- ty« of the same, Royalties, Rights of raising Monies, making Leagues and Alliances, of building and possessing Fortifications; in fine, all those Rights and Prerogatives whatsoever that his Highness did hold and enjoy before and after the Treaties of Westphaly, and of the North, to the Year 1675; as likewise whatever his Highness may claim by the Pacification of Fountainble.au; the Conditions and Contents of which Treaties are confirmed hereby: And also his Royal Majesty will restore to his Highness's Officers and Subjects ail their Goods and Debts.

3. Whereas his Highness, amongst other Demands, hath required, That his Royal Majesty would free the Islands of Femeren, together with the Governments of Steinhorst, Tremsbuttell, and Trittau, from a Mortgage, pay that Sum of Money they are engaged for, and restore them, without auy Charge, to his Highness: His

Royal

11 W. III. 13° Januarii.

u9

Royal Majesty, to give the greater Mark of his Favour to his Highness, as being nearly related to him in Blood and Affinity, doth give up the Mortgage, and remit the Action he hath against the Government of Triitau; and restores it, with its Dependencies: But, as to what concerns the Island of Femeren, and the Governments of Trmbuttdl and Steinhor&t, these being not in the Hands of his Majesty, but of his Royal Highness Prince George of Denmark; his Imperial Majesty, and their Electoral Highnesses of Saxony and Brandenburgh, in Quality of Mediators for composing these Differences, to the end that Peace and Tranquillity may the better be established and settled in the Northern Kingdoms, and the Circle of Loner Saxony, it being of great Importance to the publick Good, that it should subsist inviolably, they have undertaken to find out such means to make Satisfaction to his Royal Highness for that Sum of Money for which lie holds those Places, without any Charge or Prejudice to his Royal Majesty; as likewise to obtain the Consent of his said Royal Highness, That the said Island and Governments be restored again to his Highness the Duke of Holstein, exempt and free from the Debt and Mortgage they formerly lay under.

4. On the other Side, his Highness doth renounce all Actions and Pretensions he might have, not only against his Royal Majesty, for having detained his Dominions for some time, and enjoyed the Revenues thereof; but also doth release, and wholly desists irom, those Proceedings he had obtained from the Imperial Chamber against the House of the Dukes of Holst ein-Floen.

5. As to what belongs to Unions, Family Agreements, and other Conventions made to the Year 1675 \ as also the Communion; the Custom used to that Day shall remain in Force, no less than what hath been expressly and literally determined, in relation to this Matter, by the Treaties at IVcstphaly, of the North, and of Fountainbleau; and whatsoever remains, and is unreceived, of the Revenues of the Chamber, or Contributions in his Highness's Dominions, shall by no means be demanded from his Royal Majesty.

6. They do remit other Grievances to be made up in a friendly Transaction; and, if that doth not succeed, they leave it to the Law: And neither Party shall undertake any thing, by way of Force, against what is above settled.

7. The Ratifications of this Agreement shall be exchanged here at Altenay Fourteen Days after the Subscribing of it; and the Agreement shall immediately, or, at furthest, within Eight Days after the Exchange, be strictly put in Execution, bona fide, and without Delay.

In Witness whereof Two Copies of the same Tenor, subscribed and sealed, have been delivered to each Party.

Done at.Altena the 20th Day of June, in the Year 1689.

The said Copy of his Majesty's Guarantee of the Treaty of Altena.

WILLIAM the Third, by the Grace of God, of England, Scotland, France, and Ireland, King, Defender of the Faith, &c. To all, to whom these Presents shall come, Greeting. Whereas the late ‘ Differences arisen between our Good Brother the King of Denmark and Norway, and the Duke of Holstein Slesrcick, have been adjusted and composed by a Treaty concluded at Altena the 20th Day of June last past; whereby likewise an everlasting and firm Friendship and Union is settled and renewed between the said King of Denmark and Norway, and the said Duke of Holstein, and their Successors; a Copy of which Treaty, translated out of the German Language, in which it was signed, into Latin, does here follow;

Notum sit omnibus, See.

And whereas it is of very great Importance for the Good and Benefit of Christendom, and for maintaining in Peace and Tranquillity the Kingdoms and States in the North, That the said Treaty should be inviolably Vol 13.

kept and observed: We have thought fit, for that Rea- Treaty of sons, and in regard of the Friendship and Affection which Altena, We bear unto the said King and Duke, to grant our Guarantee of the same; that so it may appear how ready and desirous We are to contribute our Endeavours, for preserving and maintaining that Part of Christendom in Peace and Quietness: And we do accordingly, by these Presents, give and grant our Guarantee of the said Treaty, concluded at Altena between the King of Denmark and Norway, and the Duke of Holstein Sleswick, and of every Article therein contained: And We do hereby promise, and engage our Royal Word, That Wrc will employ our best Endeavours to prevent any Violation or Infringement thereof; and not only interpose our Offices* wherever it shall be necessary for this End, but also make use of our Forces, if need be, in Conjunction with those of the Party injured, and with those of our Allies, who shall likewise be concerned in this Affair, against all such as shall, by open Force or Violence, attempt any thing against the said Treaty; which We will preserve, as far as in us lies, according to the true Intent and Meaning thereof. In Witness whereof, we have caused our Great Seal of England to be affixed to these Presents.

Given at our Court at Whitehall, the 30th Day of January 1689-90, in the First Year of our Reign.

WILLIAM R.

The said 6th and 7th Articles of the Treaty of Marriage between the Prince and Princess of Denmark.

Article the 6th.

The aforesaid King of Denmark and Norway, and his Brother Prince George, by their respective Commission granted, agree and consent, That, Five Months after the Marriage already designed is solemnized, they shall constitute, and, according to the Laws of Denmark, ascertain, and confirm, for a Dowry, a certain Revenue, of the yearly Value of 25,000 Crowns, out of the Government of Wahrenburgh, and the Isle of Femeren, to the Use and Benefit of the said Prince Geflrge, and Princess, during their Lives: And in case the said Prince George shall die first, the full Revenue of the aforesaid Government of Wahrenburg, and of the Island of Femeren, with all the Rights which the Prince now enjoys, shall belong to the Princess during her Life.

Article 7th.

And whereas the most Serene King of Great Britain, and the Duke of York, have promised, That all the Estate, which the said Princess brought with her, shall descend to the Children which the Prince shall have by the Princess; in like manner the most Serene King of Denmark and Noruwy agrees, on his Part, and the said Prince George promises, That all the Estate of the said Prince shall remain in the Possession of the Children born of the said Prince and Princess: Provided nevertheless, that the Succession thereto shall be according to the Laws of Denmark; that is to say, That a Son shall always have Double the Portion of a Daughter.

A Petition of the Merchants and Traders to Newfound- Salt Duties. land, and in the Herring-fishery, living in Biddejord, in Devon, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That, by several Acts of Parliament, there is a Duty of 6s.- 8 d. per Bushel laid upon all Salt imported, payable* within Six Months, unless exported again within that time; for Payment whereof, the Petitioners give Bonds at the Custom-house: But, by reason of the Shortness of the Time for Payment, the Petitioners are greatly prejudiced in their Trade; for that, when any Salt is imported after March, they cannot again export it till February following; so that their Bonds, being thereby forfeited, are often put in Suit against them: And praying, That the Time may be enlarged for discharging the said Duties.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Avon A Petition of the Grand Jury, impanelled to serve for

Navigation, the Body of the County of Wilts, at the General Quarter Sessions of the Peace held at Salisbury in and for the said County, on die 10th Day of January 1699; together with the Justices of the Peace, Gentlemen, and other Freeholders there; was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Bill depending in the House, for making the Act for making the River Avon navigable from Christ Church, to the City of New Sarum more effectual, may be of great Advantage to the Country, by giving such Power to the Commissioners of the said Navigation as Commissioners of Sewers have for removing Obstructions, and preventing Inundations of the said River, whereby the Owners and Occupiers of the Lands bordering thereon have suffered great Damages; and that their Power be extended to several Parts of the several Rivers in and about Salisbury, running into the stud River; and also that the Undertakers of the Navigation may not be suffered to mitigate the Fines imposed by the Commissioners; without which Restraint, the Petitioners are well assured, the Powers already granted the Commissioners by the former Act will become ineffectual: And praying, That the said additional Powers may be inserted in the said Bill.

The House resumed the adjourned Debate of Yester- Privilege-day, upon the Report relating to the Letter touching the Letter. Charge of the Committee Rooms.

Ordered, That it be referred to the Committee of Privileges and Elections to examine the Matter of the said Report, so far as the same relates to the Honour of the House, and of the said Committee; and report the same, with their Opinion therein, to the House.

Navigation. inquire for the Body of the County of Wilts, at the

General Quarter Sessions of the Peace, held at the City of Salisbury the l oth Day of January 1699; together with the Justices of the Peace, Gentlemen, and other Freeholders, then and there assembled; was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Petitioners conceive, the Bill depending in the House, for making the River Avon navigable from Bristol! to Bath, will great.. lessen the Markets in the County of Wilts; and consequently lessen the Value of Lands there; the City of Bath being supplied by the Growth and Product of those Lands, in great measure; which the Passing of the said Bill will Obstruct: And praying, That the said Bill may not pass;

it being such a Prejudice and Discouragement to the Inhabitants of Wilts, that their Damage will be much more considerable, than any Persons or Places can be advantaged by it.

presented to the House, and read; ....

since the late Act of Parliament for the more effectual prohibiting the Importation of foreign Bone-lace, the Petitioners have found a great Increase of their Trade, to the Employment of the Poor; and that above 600 Persons in Shafton wholly depend on the said Manufacture; so that, if the said Act should be repealed, their Livelihood will be taken from them, and the Substance of the said Corporation will not be sufficient to supply the Wants of their Poor: And praying, That the said Act may be therefore continued.

A Petition of all the Magistrates, save One, all the Ditto. Common Council, and the greater Number of the free Burgesses, of the said Borough of Clifton-Dartmouth-Hardnesse, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That it hath been the ancient Usage of the said Corporation for the Magistrates, or first *12 Masters, or the greater Number of them, with the Mayor, to make Freemen; which, by Vote of this House in 1689, wfits declared to be the Right of the said Magistrates, or Masters: Yet one Joseph Bully, the last precedent Mayor, with one John Whit row, a Magistrate, on the 25 July last, on Pretence of a Mandanms out of the King's Bench Court, swore 13 Freemen of the said Borough, though protested against by all the rest of the Magistrates; by which means Whit row, in a few Days after, not only got himself to he elected Mayor, and other annual Officers of his Party chosen, but did not doubt to make himself, or whom he pleased, a Parliament-man for the said Borough, in the room of Sir Joseph Hern, then dead; since which Whitrow is also dead: And though the said Bully hath been served with several Mandamuses to swear one Caleb Rocket Mayor, and other Officers, who were duly elected; yet he refuseth so to do, on Pretence he was not personally served with the said Mandamus; nor indeed could he, because he absconded till after the Returns; by which Means he not only hopes to evade the due Course of the Law, but to keep the said Rocket, and other Officers, from their respective Offices: And praying the Consideration of the House in the Premises, and Relief therein.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A PETITION of the Adventurers, Miners, and Avon Workmen in the Coal-mines, within his Majesty's Navigation, Manors of Stratton super Fosse, and Farrington Gurney,

Parcel of the Duchy of Cornwall, in the County of Somerset, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth,

That the Petitioners hold several Coal-mines within the said Manors, by Grants from the Crown, under great Fines, and annual Rents; have been at great Charges in opening the Mines, and making Engines for draining the Water; and daily employ Hundreds of poor People in the said Works, and carrying Coals, on Horses, about into the Country, whose sole Livelihood depends thereon: But the Bill depending in the House for making the River Avon navigable from Bristoll to Bath, if it should pass, will utterly destroy the said Mines, and undo the said poor People: And praying, That they may be heard by Counsel against the said Bill.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the Committee, to whom the said Bill is committed: And that the Petitioners be heard by their Counsel, before the said Committee, thereupon.

OM East A Petition of the Governor and Company of MerA-Coiu" chants of London, trading into the East Indies, was pre-y' sented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Petitioners have, of iong time, been incorporated; and have considerable Estates, and great Privileges, in India; and have been at great Expence in building and maintaining Forts and factories there i But, in 1693, an Advantage was taken of the Petitioners Non-payment of a rJ ax charged upon their whole Stock on the 25th of March; which was an Holiday, and the Exchequer not open; Vet this was insisted on as a Forfeiture of the Petitioners Charter; And* in 1693, his Majesty granted them a itew Charter, with all their former Privileges; And by another Charter, of the l ith of November 1693, pursuant to the Resolutions of the House of Commons, the Sum of 744,000l. was subscribed and paid, as an additional Stock for carrying on the Trade, by above 800 new Adventurers; who, by Losses at Sea and Taxes, have had no Benefit by their Subscriptions; In which last Charter is a Proviso) That the Company should submit to such Regulations as his Majesty should appoint by tha 29th of September then next: And by another Charter, of the 28th of September 1694, it was declared, That if it should be made appear to their Majesties, that the said Charters, granted to the said Company, were unprofitable to their Majesties, or the Realm; then, after Three Years Warning, the said Letters Patents were to cease; and the Company to be no longer a Corporation;

That, by a late Act for raising Tw o Millions upon a fund, for Payment of Annuities; and for settling the Trade to the East Indies; it is enacted, That all Persons, Bodies Politick and Corporate, except the Bank of England\ who by themselves, or any in Trust for them, x should subscribe any Sum of Money, should receive pro-poitionable Annuities; and might trade yearly for so much as they subscribe, and pay to his Majesty; which Act does not determine the Petitioners Corporation; but permits them to trade for what they subscribe: That the Petitioners, at a General Court, the 3 July 1698, impowered Mr. John Du Bois, their Cashier, to subscribe 3 i 5,000 /.; which he did; and the same has been paid to his Majesty: But, the same Day the Subscription was made, the Petitioners were served with Notice, under his Majesty's Sign Manual, to dissolve their Corporation after Three Years: And, on the 27th of October following, the same Notice was served on them by Privy Seal: And the Petitioners prayed to be heard against passing the said Notice; and "desired to enter Caveats at the proper Offices; but they were not admitted; and doubt not, if they could have been heard, to have made it appear, That their being a Corporation is, and has been, profitable to his Majesty, and this Realm:

That the said new Subscription, of 315,000l. is the Property of above 1,200 Families; who therefore cannot manage that Trade, whereunto they are intjtled, but in a Corporation; nor can the Petitioners, unless they are so continued, compel their Factors or Agents to render them any Account, or make them Returns of their Estate; which will not only ruin the Petitioners in their Fortunes, but disable them to pay their Debts: And praying, That their Case may be taken into Consideration; and that, for the Preservation of their Estates, the Payment of their Debts, and the Management of their said Subscription, they may be continued a Corporation, in such manner as to the House shall seem meet.

A Petition of the Gentlemen, Merchants, Clothiers, Fullers, and others the most considerable Traders in the Woollen Manufactures, in and about the City of Exon, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Petitioners observing by the Votes of this House, that Leave is given to bring in a Bill for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company, they were exceedingly surprised, having never heard of any Petition from Exon for that Purpose; which was obtained in a clandestine Manner, they who got it well knowing the now Petitioners would have opposed it, as they have often done; for that Experience shews, that the Trade in the Woollen Manufactures best flourisheth with Freedom; which occasions many Buyers a current Price, and speedy Payment for them; and this hath induced the House to discourage all Monopolies, as being against Law, and destructive to the Rights and Liberties of the Subject: And praying, That their Trade may remain free, and unrestrained, from the private Interest of the Hamborough Company.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the said Bill be read a Second time.

Ditto. That the Petitioners find by Experience, that, since the Trade in the Woollen Manufactures hath been encouraged with a general Freedom, it hath much more enlarged itself, than when confined to tl*e narrow Limits of the Hamborough Company; which Freedom hath advanced the Markets here, by the Number of Buyers, and a current Price: And praying, That the Bill in the House for the better Encouraging and Settling

the Trade of the Hamborough Company.....; but

that that Trade may remain unrestrained, as it now is.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the said Bill be read a Second time.

Dm, A Petition of the Gentlemen, Merchants, Clothiers, Fullers, and others the most considerable Traders in the W;oollen Manufactures, in and about the Town and Parish of Ashburton, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That, there being a Bill in the House for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company, the Petitioners shew, that Experience demonstrates, that the Trade in the Woollen Manufactures, now unconfined, doth best diffuse itself through all the Markets of Europe, the many Buyers causing a current Price, and speedy Payment for them; which hath enabled the Petitioners not only to support their own Families, but to keep many poor People at Work: And praying, That the said Trade may remain freed from obliging the private Interest of the Hamborough Company.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table uiitil the said Bill be read a Second time.

A Petition of the Traders, Shipmasters, Shipwrights, and Mariners, of the Town and Parish of Topsham, on behalf of themselves, and other Places adjacent, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That, during the late ... the Petitioners lost above a Hundred Sail of Ships; and since the Peace was concluded, and the free Exportation of the Woollen Manufactures, have had several Ships employed in carrying great Quantities thereof to Hamborough: But, the Petitioners finding, by the printed Votes, that this House hath given Leave to bring in a Bill for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company, upon a Petition from the City of Exeter;, they believe the Petition was clandestinely obtained, they never hearing thereof, though frequently at Exon: And for that they conceive the said Bill will destroy their Navigation to Germany, they pray, That the Freedom of Trade in the Woollen Manufactures may be continued, as now established by Law.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table' until the said Bill be read a Second time.

A Petition of the High Sheriff, several other Gentlemen, Clothiers, and others concerned in and for the Woollen Manufactory in the County of Somerset, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That Foreigners, having of late Years been permitted to export our Woollen Manufactures beyond Sea, upon equal Terms with English Merchants, have gotten most of that Trade into their own Hands; whereby they have gained Opportunities of causing our Manufactures to be debased, and exported almost unmanufactured; of governing our Markets; and making long Payments; and imposing other Hardships and Hazards upon the Woollen Manufactures: And praying, That Provision may be made for encouraging his Majesty's natural-born Subjects to export our Woollen Manufactures to Germany, and keeping that Trade from falling into the Hands of Foreigners.

Mr. Conyers, according to Order, reported, from the Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider of the Supply to be granted to his Majesty, the Resolutions, which they had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read; and are as follow; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding 300,000 /. be granted to his Majesty, for maintaining Guards and Garisons, for the Year 1700.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, that Half-pay be allow ed, for the Year 1700, to the disbanded Officers, not otherwise provided for, according to the Vote of the 29th of April 1^99.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That Twenty-five thousand Pounds be allowed for the Office of the Ordnance, for the Year 1700.

The said Resolutions, being severally read a Second time, were, upon the Question severally put thereupon, agreed unto by the House.

Resolved, That this House will upon Thursday Morning next, resolve itself into a Committee of the whole House, to consider of Ways and Means for raising the Supply granted to his Majesty.

Sir Rowland Gxvyn, according to Order, reported, from the Committee of Privileges and Elections, the Matter, as it appeared to them, specially, touching the Election for the Borough of Thetford in the County of Norfolk; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

Upon the Petition of Edmund Soame Esquire, complaining of an undue Election and Return of James Sloane Esquire to serve for the said Borough:

The said Committee, before they came to any Resolution upon the Merits of the Election, directed the following Fact to be reported for the Judgment of the House:

That the Petitioner's Counsel insisted, That several Persons ought to be added to the Petitioner's Poll, who offered to vote for the Petitioner, and w>ere refused by llie Mayor; viz. Edward Freeman, and others:

That the Fact appeared to be thus: The Right of Election was agreed to be in the Mayor, Ten capital Burgesses, and 20 Common Councilmen:

That Edward Freeman was removed from his being a Common Councilman, because he had not signed the Association within the time prescribed by the Act; and another was sworn into his Place. Freeman himself, being examined, said, That he signed the voluntary Association; and had also signed the Association, according to the Act; but could not say whether it was before or after the Election: That he never refused to sign the Association: And, if he did not sign it in time, it was because no Session was held, at which he could regularly do it; and that he was out of Town, when it was done by the others: And that the Petitioner's Counsel further insisted, That,

if the said Freeman had not subscribed the Association in time, those who voted for the hitting Member wire. guilty of the same Fault:

That thereupon the Sitting Member's Counsel, by way of Answer to the said Objection, and to justify the Sitting Member's Voters, produced the Sessions Roll, whereon the Corporation had signed; which is introduced in these Words;

" Borough of Thetford: At a general Quarter Scssions of the Peace, holden for the Borough aforesaid,

" at the Guild-hall of the said Borough, upon Monday " the 22d Day of June, in the 8th Year of the Reign " of King William the II Id, and in the Year of our " Lord 1696, and so continued, by several Adjourn-u meats, until the 3d Day of August then next follow-"ing; the Association underwritten was subscribed to,

" by the several Persons as underwritten, according to an Act of Parliament, made in the 7th and 8th Years of " the feeign of the present King William, intituled, An Act for the better Security of his Majesty's lloyal " Person and Government:"

That the Sitting Member's Counsel offered to prove by Witnesses, That the said Persons had subscribed the Association in time, according to the said Act of Parliament: But, that Sort of Evidence being objected to, the Committee ordered the special Matter of Fact to be reported to the House.

Ordered, That the Merits of the said Election, together with the Matter of the said Report, be heard at the Bar of this House, upon Friday Morning next.

Ordered, That the Report relating to the Committee a Report dc-Room be made Tomorrow Morning. /eried.

A Petition of John Hudson Esquire, late Comptroller Ditto, of his Majesty's Field and Town Hospitals in Flanders, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth,

That every Year, during the War, he had several Thousands of Sick and Wounded under his Care, of which Trust he faithfully acquitted himself; in Consideration whereof, his Majesty last year ordered him to be inserted in the List of Officers then out of Employ, w'ho were to have Half-pay: And praying, in regard his Health, and, more, his small Fortune, is'impaired in his said Service, he may be added to the List of Officers that have Halfpay, until otherwise provided for.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table, with the other Petitions relating to Half-pay.

A Petition of William Ber, Captain in Brigadier Langstons former Regiment of Horse, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That, upon incorporating the said Regiment into other Regiments of Horse in Flanders, in 1692, the Officers were ordered to do Duty with the other Officers of Horse, and receive like Subsistence to the 23 of February 1697; That this House, the last Session, only providing for those Officers that were actually in Commission, and disbanded since the Conclusion of the Peace; the Petitioner is thereby not only wholly unprovided for, but rendered unqualified for Preferment till all the other Captains of Horse in Half-pay are provided for; though he was continually in Service to the Conclusion of the Peace; was the First Captain in the said Regiment when it was incorporated, having had his Commission from his Majesty when at Exeter, at the time that Regiment marched first into his Service; and for that the Petitioner is the only Officer of the said Regiment unprovided for: And praying the House to put him on the same Foot with those English Officers, with whom he served during the Course of the whole War.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table, with the other Petitions relating to Half-pay.

And the Petition was read; setting forth, That King Edward the 11 Id, by his Charter, inter al. granted to the Petitioners, That no Market should thenceforth be granted within Seven Miles in Circuit of the said City; and several Persons, in sundry Reigns, have endeavoured to obtain Patents for erecting of Markets for live Cattle within that Distance, who, upon hearing the Petitioners, have, from time to time, been prevented; but Sir Nathanael Curzon and John Kent Esquire, having lately erected a Market in Great for the Sale of live

Cattle, under Colour of seme Grants from the late King James, the Petitioners brought a Scire facias to reverse those Grants; and, to obstruct their Proceedings thereon, the said Sir Nath, and Mr. Kent have petitioned this House, as the Petitioners conceive: And praying, That they may be heard by their Counsel what they have to offer in relation to the Matters alleged in the said Petition of Sir Nath. Cursonand M r. Kent.

Thetford Then the House proceeded to the hearing the Matter Election. touching the Election for the Borough of Thetford in the County of Norfolk:

And the Counsel for EdmundSoame Esquire, the Petitioner, and for James Sloane Esquire, the Sitting Member, were called in; and heard; and several Witnesses examined on both Sides.

And then they withdrew.

And a Motion being made, and the Question being put, That James Sloane Esquire, in treating the Corporation of Thetford in the County of Norfolk, has been guilty of a Breach of the late Act of Parliament for preventing Expences in Elections;

The House divided.

The Yeas go forth.

Tellers for the Noes,|JJj] } 11

So it was resolved in the Affirmative.

Then the Question being put, That James Sloane Esquire is duly elected a Burgess to serve in this present Parliament for the Borough of Thetford in the County of Norfolk;

It passed in the Negative.

Resolved, That the said Election is a void Election. Ordered, That Mr. Speaker do issue his Warrant to the Clerk of the Crown, to make out a new Writ, for the Electing a Burgess to serve in this present Parliament for the Borough of Thetford in the County of Norf olk, in the room of James Sloane Esquire, who is adjudged to be unduly elected.

Committee*. Ordered, That all Committees be adjourned.

And then the House adjourned till Tomorrow Morning, Eight a Clock.

Hamborough A PETITION of divers Masters of Ships, at or Company, fx. near Kingston upon Hull, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the taking off Aliens Duties, and for want of a sufficient Support for English Merchants, hath given great Advantage to neighbouring Nations; who are so far Masters of our Trade, that very little English Shipping is employed to the East Country, Germany, Hamborough, Holland, and Flanders; to the great Discouragement of Navigation, and English Seamen, who might be therein employed, and be near at home, upon all Occasions, to serve their Country: And praying the House to establish the Hamborough and Eastland Companies, as the Means to restore and support the English Navigation to the Parts aforesaid.

Vol. 13.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the Bill for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company be read a Second time.

A Petition of the Dyers and Olothworkers in the City Hamborough of London was presented to the House, and read; setting Company, forth, That formerly, when the Hamborough Company flourished, our Woollen Manufactures were exported in great Quantities, dyed and dressed here; but, since Foreigners have had a Freedom to export the same, they have, by Degrees, encouraged the Dyeing thereof abroad; and at length, by Help of the ^reat Drawback on Dyeing-wares, will deprive the Petitioners of that Part of their Trade: And praying, That the Bill in the House for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Ham-borough Company may pass, for the Encouragement of English Merchants to export our Manufactures.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the said Bill be read a Second time.

A Petition of divers Packers, Setters, Tillet-painters, Ditto. Callenders, and Seal-makers, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That, since Foreigners have gotten the greatest Share of the Trade of exporting the English Woollen Manufactures to Germany, they have exported them almost wholly unmanufactured in the Way of the Petitioners Trade, to their great Impoverishment, which used formerly to be manufactured here; and that Trade might be regained, as the Petitioners conceive, if Encouragement were given to English Merchants to export our Woollen Manufactures to Germany: And praying, That the Bill, depending in the House, for the better Fncou-ragement and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company, may pass, for that Purpose.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the said Bill be read a Second time.

A Petition of the Bay-makers, Say-rnakers, and Per- Ditto, petuana-makers, of Colchester, and others concerned in the W oollen Manufactures there, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Poor, for above 20 Miles round, have their chief Dependence upon making the said Manufactures; which, for many Years past, have been sent to Holland, and thence conveyed, and vended in Germany; which Trade has been very beneficial to the Petitioners: But there being a Bill in the House, for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company, whereby all Persons trading to Germany must be admitted into that Company, and consequently subject to their By-laws, and probably they not contented to trade for so little Profit as the Petitioners, the Prices upon Goods will lie advanced in foreign Parts, the Consumption here lessened, the Poor want Employment, and it will put Foreigners upon all TV ays possible of setting up our Manufactures there: And praying the refore, That the said Bill may not pass.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the said Bill be read a Second time.

Silk Manu- A Petition of the Minister, Churchwardens, Overseers,

facture. and other Inhabitants, of the Parish of St. Leonard's, Shoreditch, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That, by reason of the great Decay of the Silk Manufactory, great Multitudes of People residing in the said Parish, whose sole Dependence was on the Silk Weavers and Throwers, are become an insupportable Burden to the Parish: And praying, That the Weavers and Throwers of Silk may be so relieved, that the Poor may be thereby employed, and the Petitioners eased.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the Committee of the whole House, w ho are to . consider further of the State and Condition of the Trade of . England; and particularly, to consider of the encouraging and improving the Manufactures of this Kingdom*.

Ditto. A Petition of the Rector, Vestry, and Churchwardens,

and Overseers, and other Inhabitants, of the Parish of St. Botolph's, Bishopsgatewithout, was presented to the House,

and read; setting forth, That great Numbers of People inhabit within the said Parish, whose chief Dependence is upon the Silk Manufactory. either from the Silk YY'eavers, or Silk Throwers; whose Trades are so greatly decayed, that the Petitioners indigent Neighbours are become an insupportable Burden to them: And praying, That the House will grant such Relief to the said Weavers and Throwers, as their Poor may again be employed.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the Committee of the whole House, who are to consider of the State and Condition of the Trade of England; and particularly to consider of the encouraging and improving the Manufactures of this Kingdom.

Woollen A Petition of the Clothiers in and about the Town of

Manufacture, Froome, in the County of Somerset, in behalf of themselves and many Hundreds of poor People depending on them, and their Trade, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Cloathing Trade of England is very much lessened and decayed by the great Exportation of our Wool; the late Prohibition of them in Flanders; by the high Duties on Oil, Soap, and Dyeing-stuff, whereby Foreigners undersell the English, they paying no such Duties; by the excessive Straining of our Cloth, which brings a Discredit upon it abroad; and by the great Numbers of other Tradesmen setting up the Cloathing Trade, imposing Hardships on the Labourers therein: And praying the Consideration of the House in tire Premises, and Relief therein.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the Committee of the whole House, who are to consider of the State and Condition of the Trade of England; and particularly to consider of the encouraging and improving the Manulactures of this Kingdom.

Transport A Petition of William Besaick Master, and Richard Debt. Holder Merchant, both of them Part-owners of the Ship

Mary, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the said Ship was hired, by the Commissioners for Transportation, in January 1693, and appraised upon Oath at 731/. 5s. and employed to transport about 290 Officers and Foot Soldiers, of Colonel Hamilton's Regiment, from Deptford to Os tend; where lying at Anchor to get into that Harbour, the Officers, being very impatient to get on shore, commanded the Mariners to cut her Cables; but they refused, knowing the Danger of turning her in to Shore, and persuaded them to stay till the next Tide; which they would not: But one Captain Caine, the chief Officer on board, commanded the Soldiers to cut the Cables; which so soon as they had done, the said Ship

drove ashore, and was utterly lost, but all the Men saved:

That Berwick petitioned his Majesty for Satisfaction; who referred the Matter to the Transport Commissioners; who reported the Matter, as aforesaid; and that the Owners ought to have Satisfaction: Yet the said Commissioners have omitted to insert the Petitioners Debt in the Accounts of the Debt due for Transport Service, which they have delivered in to this House: And praying, That the Petitioners Debt may be paid with the rest of the Transport Debt.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the Committee of the whole House, who are to consider further of the Supply to be granted to his Majesty.

A Petition of the Dyers in and about the Cities of - Duties m don and Westminster, and Borough of Southwark, was pre- Dye-stuff*, sented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the high Duties on Dye-stuff greatly discourages the Dyeing Trade in general; for that Foreigners have the same much cheaper, by reason of their own small Customs, and great Drawbacks from hence; whereby they are enabled to undersell the Petitioners; which, if not prevented, will shortly destroy the Dyers Trade, both at home and abroad:

And praying, That the High Duties upon Dye-stuff may be taken off, so that thereby the Petitioners may work as cheap as other Nations, and redeem their lost Trade.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Copy of an Order for fitting out the Ship Dolphin.

Admiralty Office, 29th June 98.

Gentlemen,

We do hereby desire and direct you to cause his Majesty's Step the Dolphin, at Portsmouth, to be, with all possible Dispatch, fitted out to Sea for a foreign Voyage, and manned With the lowest Complement of Men: And you are to order the Company of the said Ship to be borne and victualled aboard One of the Ships in ordinary at Portsmouth, during the Dolphins refitting. So we remain

Your affectionate Friends,

Ntny Board. II. Priest mart,

R. Rich,

A Copy bf an Order for putting the Officers and'Com-patiy of the Dolphin on board -some Ship in ordinary at Portsmouth, till they are paid oft*; and fitting the Dolphin for Sea; according to former Orders.

Admiralty Office, 18 July 1698.

Gentlemen,

Whereas We have lately granted a Commission for Captain Hunter to be Captain of his Majesty's Ship the Dolphin; we do hereby desire and direct you to cause Captain Humph. Bloftier, her late Commander, and all the Officers and Company belonging to the said Ship, excepting Captain Hdntcr, and the We mint Officers, and their allowed Servants, to be put aboard some One of

Will Culliford, Inspector General.

his Majesty's Ships in ordinary at Portsmouth, which you shall think most convenient, and borne there, both in Wages and Victuals, in the same manner as they were in the Dolphin, until they shall be paid off: And that the said Ship Dolphin be fitted for the Sea with all possible Dispatch, according to our late Orders to you. So we remain

Your affectionate Friends,

Extract of a Letter from Mr. Secretary Vernon, dated the 16th January 1698, about Instructions for Captain Hunter.

The inclosed Request Of the Earl of Macclesfield having been laid before the King; his Majesty commands me to send the same to your Lordships; and to acquaint you with his Majesty's Pleasure, That Captain Hunter being designed to command his Majesty's Ship the Dolphin, in the Discovery of a considerable Wreck in the West Indies, his Majesty woukl have you consider of such Instructions as may be proper to be given $0 the said Captain for the due Performance of his Service.

A true Copy,

J. Burchett.

Instructions to Captain Hunter, Commander of his Majesty's Ship Dolphin, upon the Discovery of Wrecks in the West Indies, proposed by the Gentlemen concerned in the said Wrecks.

After yoQ have received your Orders from the Right Honourable the Lords "Commissioners for executing the 'Office of Lord High Admiral, you are to make the ‘best of yo'Ur Way to Barbadoes; mid proceed from thence, with all Expedition. You are, in the First Place, to use 'the best of your Endeavours, to find out, and take up, such Wrecks as are contained and described in the^eral Papers you have left in the Hands of Samuel OYtwerse Esquire, for the Use and Benefit of all the Parties concerned; and afterwards such* other Wrecks as you shall receive Intelligence of, pursuant to our Indenture with Sir James Houblon, and Company, by virtue of Letters Patents to his Grace the Duke of Schonberg and Leinster, between Twelve Degrees South and Forty Degrees North Latitude.

You are "also, with the Consent of such Agent as we shall appoint, to contract with any Person or Persons for any new Discoveries within our due Limits, other than what is contained in your above mentioned Papers; and to allow him or them^uch n Share, not exceeding a Tenth Part, for such their Discovery, as you Two shall agree upon; which Share or Proportion, so contracted for between you Two and such Discoverer, is to be deducted out of the net Proceed of the sail Discovery.

You are to keep a true Journal of your Proceedings; and an exact Account of all Treasure, &c. by you to> be taken up; and to transmit the same to us, signed# by

yourself,

o

It W. III.

27° yanuariu

»5S

yourself, and attested by his Majesty's Agent and ours, from time to time, by all Opportunities.

You are also to go or send to the Island of Jamaica once in Two or Three Months, Wind and Weather permitting, there to inquire for and receive such further Orders and Directions as we, from time to time, shall send you; which you are punctually to observe, having a due Regard to the Orders of the Right Honourable the Lords of the Admiralty; and also, by all Opportunities, to transmit us a true Account of all your Proceedings and Transactions relating to your Undertaking: And, in case of your Death, which God prevent, you are to leave all the Papers relating to this Undertaking with our Agent then on board you, the better to enable him to prosecute the said Undertaking, under the Command of such Persons as the said Right Honourable the Lords of the Admiralty shall appoint to succeed you.

You are not to inspect the Papers or Accounts of the Two Persons appointed Agents for the King, and the Persons concerned, without their Consent; and to permit them quietly to do their Business.

A true Copy,

J. Burchett.

A Copy of Instructions to Captain Hunter, Commander of his Majesty's Ship the Dolphin, 31 January 169J-.

By the Commissioners for executing the Office of Lord High Admiral of England, Scotland, and Ireland, &c.

Whereas his Majesty hath been pleased to order, That the Ship Dolphin, under your Command, shall be fitted out for an Expedition to the West Indies, in order to the taking up several Wrecks, which are contained and described in the several Papers which you have left in the Hands of Samuel Traverse Esquire, for the Use and Benefit of the Parties concerned therein; as also such other Wrecks as you shall receive Intelligence of, pursuant to the Indentures between the said Persons, and Sir James Houblon, and Company, by virtue of Letters Patents to his Grace the Duke of Schonberg, between Twelve Degrees South and Forty Degrees North Latitude:

You are therefore hereby required and directed forthwith to proceed on this Service, with the Ship under your Command; and, with all possible Care and Diligence, put in Execution, as well the Instructions from the Persons concerned, hereunto annexed, as what further Orders and Instructions shall be given you, from time to time, by them, in the fishing for, recovering, and disposing of, all, or any Part, of the said Wrecks, as you shall recover, that so his Majesty's Share thereof may be demanded and received.

When you have done what you are able, in the Performance of this Service, you are to return, with the Ship you command, to England, calling in at Plymouth for Orders; and, if you find none there to the contrary, you are to make the best of your Way to the Downes, and remain there till further Order, giving us an Account of your Proceedings.

You are to receive on board the Ship you command, such Person as the Right Honourable the Lords of his Majesty's Treasury shall appoint to take Care of the King's Share of the Wrecks, which shall be recovered; as also such other Person as the Parties concerned in the said Wrecks shall appoint to look after and manage their Affairs; allowing them Victuals during the time they shall be aboard you, as to your Ship's Company, and bearing them as Supernumeraries on your Books.

You are, by all Opportunities you shall meet with, to send this Board an Account of your Proceedings; and, during the whole Term of the Voyage, you are to take particular Care not to annoy any o1 his Majesty's Ships, or those of his Allies, but rather tp give them what Assistance you can, without Hindrance or Prejudice to the Affair whereon you arc epiployed.

And, for the better lengthening out your Provision, you are to put the Men under your Command, when Vo.i. 13.

you come out of the Chanel, to Six to Four Mens Al-Iowance, assuring them, that they shall be punctually paid for the same at the End of the Voyage.

Dated at the Admiralty Office, the 31st of January

To Captain Collin Hunter, H. Pricslman,

Commander of his Ma- G. Roojce,

jesty's Ship Dolphin. II Houblon,

JKendall.

Extract of a Letter from Mr. Secretary Vernon, dated the 30th of January 1698.

I have laid before his Majesty your Lordship's Letter of the 23d Instant, with the inclosed Copies of Instructions for the Commander of his Majesty's Ship the Dolphin, as well from your Lordship, as from the Persons concerned in the Wrecks that are to be fished up; whereupon his Majesty hath commanded me to acquaint you,

That he approves of the said Instructions.

A true Copy,

A Petition of the English Company trading to the old East East Indies was presented to the House, and read; setting India Comfort!), That the Petitioners are the greatest Part of the Pan>T % Subscribers intitled to the sole Trade to the East Indies, after a certain time, by virtue of an Act of Parliament for raising Two Millions upon a Fund for Payment of Annuities; and the Petitioners are accordingly incorporated:

That the Old East India Company were, by the said Act, to continue their Trade to India no longer than the 29th of September 1701; according to which limited Time, and the Power reserved by his Majesty in their Charter, his Majesty sent them Notice of their Determn nation: And the Consideration, that his Majesty had no Power to erect any other Company to trade to India with a Joint Stock but the One Company aforesaid, was tire Inducement for the Petitioners to make the said Loan:

That the Petitioners are informed, the Old East Iiulia Company have petitioned this House upon divers Suggestions for continuing them a Corporation for the Management of a Subscription of 315,000l. made by Mr.

John Dubois, in Trust for them: And that the House hath given Leave to bring in a Bill for that Purpose, which is ordered a Second Reading: That the said Bill is directly contrary to the said Act of Parliament; destructive of the Petitioners Rights; and the erecting another Corporation, to trade with a Joint Stock, will be dishonourable and disadvantageous to the English Nation, and Interest in the East Indies, and other foreign Parts: And praying, That they may be heard at the Bar of the House, before the said Bill do pass.

Ordered, That the Petitioners be heard, by their Counsel, at the Bar of this House, upon Wednesday Morning next, against the Bill for continuing the Governor and Company of Merchants of London trading to the East Indies a Corporation, upon the Second Reading thereof:

And that the Counsel for the Old East India Company be heard, at the same time, for the said Bill.

A Petition of several Persons, on behalf of themselves, on and many others, who advanced to his Majesty the Sum Stone, See. of 564,700 /. upon the Credit of an Act of Parliament, made in the 6th and 7th Years of his Majesty's Reign, for granting to his Majesty certain Rates and Duties upon Stone, Glass, Earthen Wares, Coals, and Culm, for the Term of Five Years, for carrying on the War against France, impowering his Majesty to borrow' the said Sum, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth,

That, to encourage Persons to lend the said Money, there was a Clause in the said Act, Thai what should tall short to pay Principal and Interest by the said Fund, should be paid out of the next Aids to be granted by Parliament:

That, the then next Session, the Duties on Stone, Glass,

15^ 27° — 2 9s

and Earthen Wares, were appropriated for establishing a national Land Bank, and the Duty on Coals was quite taken off, without the Petitioners Consent; which would have fully paid them; so that they were left without any Security: That the next Session, in the 8th and 9th Years of his Majesty's Reign, a Duty was laid upon Leather, for Three Years, for Payment of the Petitioners; and a Clause for transferring the Deficiency, to be made good out of the First Aids to be given by Parliament: That, in the 9th and 10th Years of the King, a Duty was laid on Coals and Culm again, for raising 500,000l.: And the Petitioners then, petitioned the House, That they might be restored to their First Security; but their Petition was not received: That the Duty on Leather has not paid off any Principal for above 12 Months past, and will expire the 20th of April next; whereby the Petitioners will not have any Fund for Repayment of their said Debt; wherein, they conceive, the Credit of the Nation is highly concerned; and praying, That their Case may be taken into Consideration: And that they may be restored to their First Security; or that some other effectual Provision may be made for Repayment of their said just Debt, and Interest.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the Committee of the whole House, who are to consider of the Supply to be granted to his Majesty; to whom the Account of Deficiencies, not already provided for, is referred.

A PETITION of the Clothiers of Strozvdwater, Export and others of the County of Gloucester, was pre- Wool, sented to the House, and read; setting forth, That they conceive the Commissioners appointed, by an Act made in the First Year of his Majesty's Reign, for preventing the Exportation of Wool, were disabled from putting the same in Execution for want of a Fund to support the Charge of so great an Undertaking; but the said Commissioners, at the earnest Solicitation of the Petitioners, have, at their own Expence, done their utmost to put the Laws in Execution; and have made many considerable Seizures of Wool, and discovered many notorious Offenders; whereby the Petitioners are very sensible the Woollen Trade has received Advantage, and would receive a further Benefit, were the said Commissioners encouraged by a public Supply of a moderate Tax to be laid upon Wool, which the Petitioners w'ould willingly pay, if the House shall please to lay the same: And praying the House to take the Premises into Consideration.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Petition of the Freeholders and Inhabitants of the Town and Parish of Ring-wood, near the River Avon, in the County of Southampton, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That by an Act of Parliament'

made in the 16 and 17th Years of the Reign of King Charles the lid, for making navigable the River Avon from Christ Church to New Sarum, Undertakers were appointed to effect the same; which they have not yet done, to any Advantage to themselves, or the Country; whom they have hitherto very much injured by treading doVm the Ghiss, and spoiling the Ground near the River, without making any Satisfaction; and sometimes have gotten Decrees for their Land at an Under-value; and have procured Fines to be laid for not cutting the Weeds in the said River, though they were no Prejudice to the Undertakers, or any body else; by which, and many other causeless Pretences, the Act, which was designed to be for the Good of the Country, is converted to their Oppression; and there is a Biff in the House for making the Act, for making the River Avon navigable from Christ Church to New Sarum, more effectual; the chief Design whereof being to inlarge the Power of the Undertakers, and for the more easy Recovery of such unjust Fines and Taxes as are or shall be laid by them, the Petitioners pray, That they may be secured, and heard against the same.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the Committee, to w horn the said Bill is committed: And that the Petitioners be heard by the Committee thereupon.

A Petition of the Freeholders and Inhabitants of Sophy, Ripley, and Avon, near Christ Church, and the River Avdn, in the County of Southampton, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Undertakers for making the River Avon navigable from Christ Church to New Sancm, by an Act made in the 16 and 17th Years of King Charles the I Id, have not been able to effect the same to any Advantage; but have made the Haven worse, and committed great Injuries to Land-owners near the said River, without making any Satisfaction; and the new Undertakers have procured the Commissioners for putting the said Act in Execution to lay several unreasonable Fines on the Petitioners, and others, for not cutting the Weeds, and keeping up ancient Weirs on the River, which are no Prejudice to the Navigation; and demand Duties for exporting and importing Goods at the ancient Haven below Christ Church, to the great Oppression of the Country; and the Undertakers, finding the y are like to have no other Benefit by the said Navigation, have procured Leave to bring a Biff into the House for making the Act, for making the River Avon navigable from Christ Church to New Sarum, more effectual; the Design whereof is to impower them the more easily to recover their unreasonable Demands, and inlarge their Powers, that they may be more vexatious to the Petitioners, and the whole Country: And praying, That they may be secured against all Exactions of the Undertakers; and be heard to shew their Reasons against the said Bill.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the Committee, to whom the said Bill is committed: And that the Petitioners be heard by the Committee thereupon.

A Petition of the Merchants and others, Traders and Exporting Dealers in Wool, in and about the Town of Barnstable, Wool from was presented to the House, and read; setting forth,. m J That, notwithstanding an Act, made the last Session of Parliament, to prevent the Exportation of Wool out of the Kingdoms of Ireland and England into foreign Parts, ordering Licences to be taken from the Custom-houses in England to bring Wool hither from Ireland; yet the Government of Ireland will not permit any Wool to be loaden there, without paying 21/. 5.?. for every Thousand Stone of Wool exported thence into England; pretending such Imposition is for Licence Money and Certificates; which is contrary to Law, as the Petitioners are advised, who pay his Majesty's Customs in Ireland also: And praying, That the like Abuses may be prevented for the future, being very detrimental to the Petitioners in the Way of their Trades.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the said Committee: And that they do examine the Matter; and state the same to the House.

A Petition of the Freeholders and Inhabitants of the d Parish of Ibsly, near the River Avon, in the County of Southampton, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That an Act of Parliament was made in the 16 and 17th Years of King Charles the Second, for making the River Avon navigable from Christ Church to New Sarum, by Undertakers for that Purpose, who have not since been able to effect the same, or do any manner of Good therein, nor are ever like to do it; but have done a great many Injuries to those who have Lands near the said River, by treading down their Grass, and spoiling their Grounds, without any Satisfaction; and have laid, and demand, many unreasonable Fines and Amercements for not cutting the Weeds in the River, though they are no Prejudice to the Undertakers, or any body else; and, by many other causeless Pretences, they oppress the Country, designing to exact what they can by such unjust Means, finding the y are like to make no Advantage any other ways by the said Navigation: That there is a Bill in this House for making the said Act more effectual; which is designed only to enable the Undertakers to recover their unjust Demands more easily, and to give them further Powers on the said River; which already hath been extended to the Wrong of many People: And praying, That the Petitioners may be secured against all Demands of the said Undertakers, and be heard against the said Bill.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petition be referred to the Committee, to w hom the said Bill is committed: And that the Petitioners be heard by their Counsel, before the Committee, thereupon.

A Petition of several Traders, Masters of Vessels, and Mariners, in and near Christ Church, in the County of Southampton, was presented to the House, and read;

Vol. 13.

Setting forth, That, Time out of Mind, there has been a small Creek or Haven below the said Town, to which Three or Four small Vessels of the Petitioners, and others* belonged, for carrying Corn, and other Commodities* for the Use of the Country thereabouts, where they used a Place in Somerford Manor, by the Haven, for lading and unlading Goods; but now a small Key and Alehouse is built thereon, by Undertakers for making the River Avon navigable from Christ Church to New Sarum, by virtue of an Act of Parliament made in the 16 and 17th Years of King Charles the Second's Reign; who have also made a new Cut from the Sea to the said Haven, with Design, as pretended, to make a new and better Haven; but the Undertakers, finding the Work impossible, left the same off, and made the Haven worse, and more dangerous Passage by the new Cut, whereby the Sand is brought in, and the Haven like to be utterly spoiled for want of the Current through the Old Passage; and the Petitioners have received no manner of Advantage by what the Undertakers have done; yet they, by Colour of Orders made by their Commissioners, demand, and have sued the Petitioners for, great Duties and Fines for using the said Haven, and for not cutting the Weeds in the said River, although the Petitioners conceive it was not intended, that the Undertakers Power, by the said Act, should extend below Christ Church, where the River was navigable before: That the Bill in the House, for making the said Act more effectual, is only to enable the Undertakers to recover such their unjust Taxations, and to give them a further Power, than they had before by the said former Act: And praying, That they may be relieved against all Fines and Demands of the Undertakers, and be heard against passing of the said Bill.

Ordered, That the Consideration of the said Petitioni be referred to the Committee, to whom the said Bill is committed: And that the Petitioners be heard by their Counsel, before the Committee, thereupon.

A Petition of the Mayor, Magistrates, Common Hamborough Council, Merchants, principal Inhabitants, and others, Company* the most considerable Traders in the Woollen Manufactures in and about the Borough of Plimouth, in the County of Devon, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Petitioners finding, by the Votes of this House, That Leave is given to bring in a Bill for the supporting the Hamborough Company, they beg Leave to represent, That Experience demonstrates, that the Woollen Manufacture Trade, when attended with Freedom^ disfuseth itself through all the Markets of Europe-, for which Reason this House hath justly discouraged Monopolies; and the Petitioners have found, w hilst the Trade hath been unconfined, that many Buyers have occasioned such a current Price, and speedy Payment, as hath enabled them not only to support their own Families, and employ great numbers of the Poor, but also great. . to increase his Majesty's Revenue: And praying, that the Trade in the Woollen Manufactures may remain unconstrained, and free from obliging the private Interest of the Hamborough Company only.

Ordard, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the Bill for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company be read a Second Time.

Sir George Rook, from the Lords Commissioners of Seamen's the Admiralty, and Commissioners of the Navy, pre- Arrears* sented to the House their Report touching the Q's and R's; and also touching the Blackwell-hall Sloop: And the same are as follow; viz.

The Report about Q's and R's.

The Honourable House of Commons having been pleased to refer unto such of the Lords Commissioners of the Admiralty, and Commissioners of the Navy, as are Members of the said House, Two Petitions, presented unto them, relating to the Q's and R's put on Seamen for deserting his Majesty's Service, in order to our considering thereof, and reporting their Case; we have, in pursuance thereof, taken the same into Consideration; and do report as follows:

As to the R's;

That it hath been the Practice of the Navy, Time out of Mind, for the Commanders of his Majesty's Ships to make Men Run, who desert the Service; and that not only the Commanders of his Majesty's Ships, but likewise all the Clerks of the Cheque, and Muster-masters of the Navy, have, in all Times past, been obliged thereto by their Instructions; by which Desertions all their Wages, as w>ell for Ships they have served in formerly, so far as the same could be discovered, as for the Ships they left, have been ever reckoned to be forfeited to his Majesty; and the utmost Care injoined by the Lord High Admiral, upon all Officers concerned, to exact the same, for deterring the Seamen from leaving his Majesty's Ship's,

But Mr. Edzvards came to the Board, and acquainted them, That his Vessel was not fit to cruise on that Coast.

Whereupon the Board did resolve to employ her as a Tender on the Fleet, in regard Mr. Edwards could not be gratified in her cruising on the Coast of Sussex; those Vessels being, by Act of Parliament, appointed and employed by the Commissioners of the Customs; and therefore Orders were given for reducing her Men to the Number of Ten: But upon Mr. Edwards's Representation, That he should be exposed to the Danger of the French Coasters, it was, in August last, determined, that she should have Twelve Men.

A Petition of the Corporation of Trinity-house, in Kingston upon Hull, on the behalf of the poor, decayed, and distressed Seamen, their Widows and Children, within the Town of Hull, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That they are incorporated by several Grants; have several Rents and Revenues; and their Poor are very much increased since the War: That by an Act passed in the 9th and 10th Years of his Majesty's Reign, for erecting Work-houses in the said Town, for employing and maintaining the Poor, there are several Clauses, which tend to the Prejudice of the said Corporation; and particularly one, which enacts, That all future Charities, to be given or disposed to the Use of the said Town, or any Parish, Place, or Precinct, within the same, shall be enjoyed by the new Corporation; which Clause will totally prevent any seafaring Man, or other Person, to bequeath any Charity to Trinity-house: And praying, That a Clause may be brought in to explain so much of the said Act as relates to the Petitioners; and that they may be in the same Condition as before the making of the said Act.

Ordered, That the Committee, to whom the Bill for the more effectual Punishment of Vagrants, and sending them whither by Law they ought to be sent, is committed, have Power to receive a Clause for explaining the said Act, according to the said Petition.

A Petition of John Clements Gentleman was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Petitioner, for himself and others, is a Mortgagee of the Office of Warden of the Fleet Prison, for 2,299/. principal Money; and there being a Bill in the House for Dissolution of the Fleet Prison, whereby the Office is first to cease, and yet afterwards be sold, the Petitioner conceives, he is thereby likely to be deprived of his Security: That there is a Bill also depending in the House to dissolve the King's Bench; wherein there is a Clause, that seems to imply, that, after Sale of the Oxfordshire Estate therein mentioned, the Publick shall make good to the Mortgagee of the Kings Bench, where the said Estate shall fall short of paying; which, as is alleged, will amount to above Eleven thousand Pounds: And praying, That the Creditors of the Fleet Prison may be as amply provided for, as those of the Kings Bench; and that he may be heard by Counsel, before the Bill for the Dissolution of the Fleet Prison do pass.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the said Bill be read a Second time.

A Petition of divers Gentlemen, Merchants, Clothiers, Clothworkers, and others, in Leeds, and several Towns adjacent, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Exportation of our Woollen Manufactures w'as first attempted, and afterwards successfully carried on, by the Company of Merchants of England; but of late their Privileges have been invaded by Foreigners, upon whom a great Part of the Woollen Trade is fallen, as to Holland; and will totally be carried into foreign Parts, where it is already set up, unless some speedy Care be taken therein: And praying, That the said Company may be established and protected in their Privileges to Germany, as the only Means to prevent the said Mischiefs.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the Bill for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company be read a Second time.

The Three Votes that were impeached by the Petitioner's Counsel w ere,

William James,

Tho. Waters, and Samuel James.

The Objection to William James was, That he was an Out-Burgess.

It appeared, That the Oath'to In-Burgess and Out-

Burgess was the same: And, if an Out-Burgess came to live within the Borough, he did not take a new Oath; but the In-Burgess, and the Out-Burgess, being entered upon several Lists, such Person, coming to live within the Borough, is entered upon the List with the In-Burgess.

Mr. David Morris, Mr. Tho. Bright, Mr. Morris Pugh senior, Mr. Wm. Merrick, said, That William James lived at Mainton, Two Miles off Bishops Castle, about the time of the Election; and only came to Town, as a Journeyman Shoemaker, to work; and went Home on Saturday Nights; and was not entered among the Burgesses till after the Election, though occasionally he did Tie in Bishops Castle sometimes; and therefore they looked on him as an Out-Burgess: And that, the Day before the Election, the Mayor and others met to adjust the Right of the Electors; and it was then agreed, that William James had no Vote, being a Country-Burgess.

William Price: That Thomas Waters went Home every Saturday Night to Coltbeck, about Half a Mile off Bishops Castle', but had worked for some Years at Bishops Castle.

JOHNNiman, and Baltzer Lyell, took the Oaths appointed, in order to their Naturalization.

A Petition of the Employers of Wool-spinners and Wool-combers, inhabiting in and about the City of Canterbury, on behalf of themselves, and the great Numbers of poor People by them employed, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That Leave being given to bring in a Bill for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company, the Petitioners beg Leave to acquaint the House, That they find by Experience, That the Trade in the Woollen Manufacture does best extend itself through all the Markets of Europe, when left to its full Freedom; since which, the Petitioners have had constant Work, and competent Prices; and maintained themselves, and vast Numbers of Poor, which otherwise must have starved: And praying, That the Trade to Germany may not be restrained to the Hamborough Company only, but that it may be continued in its full Freedom.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the said Bill be read a Second time.

A Petition of the Gentlemen, Merchants, Clothiers, and other considerable Dealers in the Woollen Manufactures, at Leeds, and Parts adjacent, in the West Riding of the County of York, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth. That the House having given Leave to bring in a Bill for the Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company, the Petitioners represent, That when the Trade to Germany was limited to the Hamborough Company only, it was very prejudicial to the Cloathing Trade in general; when, on the contrary, that Trade was left to a general Liberty, it met with far greater Encouragement both at home and abroad: And praying, That the said Trade may remain unconfined, and not be again reduced to the sole Interest of the Hamborough Company.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the said Bill be read a Second time.

A Petition of divers Gentlemen and Clothiers, in and about the Cloathing Towns of Dewsborough and Mir-feild, in the West Riding of the County of York, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Exportation of our Woollen Manufactures was first attempted, and successfully carried on, by the Hamborough Company, to the great Benefit of the Nation; but, for want of sufficient Support of the said Company, Foreigners have got so great a Share of the said Trade, That it is in Danger of being lost to English Merchants; and consequently the Clothiers must lie in great Danger of having Hardships put upon them, and the Manufactures of being debased and carried into foreign Parts, by the Insight of Foreigners in the Working thereof: And praying, That the said Company may be established and protected in their Trade to Germany, under such Regulations as the House shall think fit.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the Bill for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company, be read a Second time.

A Petition of divers Gentlemen, Merchants, Clothiers, Cloth workers, Fullers, and others, in Hallifax, and Vol. 13.

Februarii. 1-73

Parts adjacent, in the West Riding of the County of York, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That though the Hamborough Company first exported our Woollen Manufactures, to the great Advantage of the Nation, into Holland and Germany, yet Foreigners have gotten the sole Trade to Holland, and are likely to get it to Germany, for want of Encouragement to the said Company; which Trade, if in the Hands of Foreigners, may occasion great Hardships to be put on the Clothiers; and by an Insight in the manner of Working, and the Opportunity of exporting our Wool, may be a Means of transplanting our Art into foreign Countries, to the total Loss thereof to this Nation: And praying, That the said Company may be protected in their Trade to Gemnany, by Act of Parliament, to prevent the said threatening Mischiefs.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the Bill for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company, be read a Second time.

A Petition of divers Gentlemen, Clothiers, and others, Hamborough principally concerned in the Woollen Manufactures, in Company. Farnlcy, Bramley, Pudsey, Cabcerly, and Idle, in the West Riding of the County of York, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Exportation of our Woollen Manufactures was at first attempted, and afterwards successfully carried on, by the Hamborough Company; but, for want of a sufficient Support, Foreigners have gotten such a Share of that Trade, that the said Company is in danger of losing their Trade to Germany, and the Woollen Manufacture in Danger of being debased, and set up in Foreign Countries: And praying,

That the said Company may be established and supported in their direct Trade to Germany, under such Regulations as the House shall think fit.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the Bill for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company, be read a Second time.

A Petition of divers Gentlemen, Clothiers, Cloth- Ditto, workers, and others, principally concerned in the Woollen Manufactures in Burstall, Little and Great Summer-sail, High Townes, Harset, Clifton, and Heaton, in the West Riding of the County of York, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Trade of the Hamborough Company, which is for the general Good of the Nation, and the Woollen Manufactures, is infringed by Foreigners, and in Danger of being' lost to English Merchants, for want of Encouragement to the said Company; and, if some Care be not taken, our Woollen Trade may be carried on in foreign Countries, where it is already begun: And praying, That the said Company may be established and protected in their Trade to Germany only, by Act of Parliament, as the only Means to prevent the ensuing Mischiefs.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table until the Bill for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company, be read a Second time.

A Petition of the Bailiffs and Burgesses, and other In- Ditto, habitants, of the Borough of Kidderminster, in the County of Worcester, being an eminent Cloathing Town, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Petitioners find by the Votes of this House, that a Bill is brought in for the better Encouraging and Settling the Trade of the Hamborough Company: And well knowing, that the Cloathing Trade was heretofore much more beneficial to the Traders therein, when it was managed by English Merchants, than now; not only in respect of the Price, but the Assurance of their Money; the Petitioners therefore pray, That the said Bill may pass, giving all Encouragement to English Merchants to export our Woollen Manufactures, by such Ways as the House shall think fit.

Assaying of Mr. Scobell reported from the Committee, to whom plate* the Petitions of the Goldsmiths of the Cities of Exeter % Chester, and Nonvich, and the Borough of Honiton, Chard, and Crewkern, were referred, That they had examined the same, and had come to a Resolution, which they had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and i§ as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That Wardens and Assay-masters be appointed in most considerable Cities and Towns of this Kingdom, for assaying all Plate, according to the present Standard; and for affixing the Britannia Mark on such Plate: And that the Goldsmiths, and Workers of Silver, in such Cities and Towns, be under such Rules and Regulations, as may prevent Abuses and Corruptions therein.

The said Resolution being read a Second time:

Resolved, That the House doth agree with the Committee in the said Resolution, That Wardens and Assay-masters be appointed in most considerable Cities and Towns of this Kingdom, for assaying all Plate, according to the present Standard; and for affixing the Britannia Mark on such Plate: And that the Goldsmiths, and Workers of Silver, in such Cities and Towns, be under such Rules and Regulations, as may prevent Abuses and Corruptions therein.

Ordered, That a Bill be brought in upon the said Resolution; and that Sir Barth. Shore and Mr. Scobell do prepare, and bring in, the Bill.
